ic.rule_summary: CRITICAL: Entergy New Orleans is regulated by the NEW ORLEANS CITY COUNCIL, not the LPSC -- a wholly separate jurisdiction. The City Council adopted its own net-metering rules in May 2007, similar in structure to (but administered independently of) the LPSC's rules: residential systems up to 25 kW, commercial/agricultural up to 300 kW. Because New Orleans regulates its own utility, the September 2019 LPSC order that moved the rest of Louisiana to avoided-cost net billing for post-2019 interconnections did NOT automatically apply here -- New Orleans customers were reported (as of the 2019 LPSC change) to still have retail net metering available, making Entergy New Orleans a materially more favorable jurisdiction within the same corporate family than Entergy Louisiana. Current City Council net metering docket status and whether it has since moved to a similar avoided-cost structure was NOT independently confirmed in this pass -- treat as a high-priority gap given the economic significance.

City purchases the customer's RECs as part of the net metering agreement (customer may instead elect to keep RECs and be paid at the avoided average energy market price at the Columbia pricing node in lieu of retail-rate netting). ic.rule_summary: DEMEC is a joint-action wholesale power agency representing 9 Delaware municipal electric departments (New Castle, Newark, Middletown, Smyrna, Clayton, Dover, Milford, Seaford, Lewes); each member municipality sets its OWN net-metering/interconnection tariff and is exempt from PSC rules per 26 Del. Following SB 298 (2022): excess kWh credits revert to the utility (no payout, no rollover) at the end of each member's annualized billing period; DEMEC's recommended (and most members') practice is an annualized period running spring-to-spring so summer-generated credits carry through winter consumption (contrast with DE Electric Coop's rockier transition, and with Delmarva which lets customers choose their own true-up month). Non-residential net-metering customers pay the full reasonable cost of any new/replacement net meter; residential customers pay up to $200 -- statewide statutory floor, but METER COST is billed directly to the customer at DEMEC members (verify this is not absorbed by any individual member as a local incentive). Utilities may consider system reliability/safety/capacity when reviewing interconnection and net-metering applications (SB 298), giving DEMEC members discretion PSC-regulated Delmarva may have less of.

ic.rule_summary: SCC Final Order (Aug. 29, 2025) largely rejected APCo's proposed net metering overhaul. APCo had sought to cut net-excess-generation compensation by ~70% (from ~8c/kWh to as low as 4.7c/kWh) and to add new grid-connection/standby charges; the SCC rejected the standby charge entirely and rejected switching from 12-month to hourly netting. Full retail 1:1 credit for self-consumed solar within the 12-month banking period is preserved. Net excess generation (true excess beyond annual consumption) is now compensated at a rate that includes REC value and exceeds the prior default PJM LMP-based avoided-cost rate. The 6% aggregate cap was retained (APCo had sought a reduction).

ic.utility_name: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
ic.rule_summary: Dominion's residential/small-C&I tariff sub-caps nonresidential systems at 1 MW (below the 3 MW statewide statutory ceiling). Following the SCC's April 30, 2026 final order (Case No. PUR-2025-00079), Dominion is rolling out a 'NEM 2.0' tariff for customers who interconnect after the order's effective date: 1:1 kWh crediting and 12-month (annual) netting are preserved, but the year-end net-excess-generation cash-out rate rises to $0.05829/kWh (includes a new $0.01/kWh credit for avoided RPS/REC compliance cost) and a $1/month administrative fee applies. The SCC rejected Dominion's proposed $100-750 application fee and its proposed 30-minute netting/dollar-based interval crediting. Pre-order NEM 1.0 customers remain grandfathered indefinitely and may switch to NEM 2.0 only if it becomes more favorable to them. Low-income customers may choose whichever tariff (legacy or NEM 2.0) is more favorable. Separately, the SCC-authorized standby charge threshold rises from 15 kW AC to 20 kW AC effective 7/1/2026 under HB 1255.

ic.utility_name: Consolidated Edison Co of New York (Con Edison)
ic.rule_summary: Follows the statewide SIR for process and timelines, but its territory is dominated by underground secondary-network and spot-network grid, which changes what interconnection actually costs. Con Edison publishes CESIR cost ranges of up to about $20,000 for inverter-based systems and about $27,000 for rotating machines. On spot/isolated networks the default is a reverse-power relay that prevents export; since 2012 Con Edison offers Communications Aided Tripping (CAT) - insensitive network-protector settings plus SCADA, anti-islanding and DNP3 telemetry - to allow export on network service, at a project cost on the order of $100,000. Con Edison states it is the only utility in the nation allowing export on network service. Interconnection portal split at 50 kW-AC (Small DG vs Large DG); for hybrid projects the portal is chosen by export capability rather than combined nameplate. 2026 Customer Benefit Contribution: net-metered PV $1.29/kW-mo residential and $1.47/kW-mo small commercial; Value Stack PV $0.65 and $1.03.
ic.ic_study_trigger_kw: In underground secondary network areas a CESIR may be required even for systems at or below 50 kW (SIR Sec I.C Exception 1); Con Edison-published CESIR cost up to ~$20,000 inverter-based and ~$27,000 rotating machine.
ic.non_export_option: Yes - reverse power relay preventing export is Con Edison's traditional approach on spot and isolated networks; CAT is the paid alternative that permits export.
ic.grid_charging_allowed: Yes - see state row. Con Edison requires charging kW (peak kW/kVA needed to charge) to be stated in the application scope of work; if it exceeds the local service, service upgrades may be required.
ic.standby_charge: Standby Service under General Rule 20, plus the Rider Q Standby Pilot Rate Program (customer-selected contract demand and As-Used demand period) and SC-11 Buy-Back Service (LBMP, grossed up by 1.066 for secondary-level deliveries). Published standby rates (as of retrieval): residential contract demand $6.05/kW plus $20 customer charge; small business $8.77/kW plus $33; large commercial low-tension under 1,500 kW $9.18/kW plus $71.
ic.standby_threshold_kw: 50 - customers with Contract Demand below 50 kW are reported exempt from mandatory Standby Service billing under General Rule 20.3, as are customers whose on-site generation nameplate is no more than 15% of maximum potential demand served from all sources. This aligns the standby threshold with the SIR's 50 kW expedited/large-project boundary. Threshold is SECONDARY-sourced - not read in the General Rule 20 tariff leaf.
ic.storage_specific_notes: Con Edison states that SC1 residential customers under 25 kW-AC and SC2 small commercial customers under 2 MW-AC who install an ESS after 2017-03-10 receive Phase One NEM compensation, and that residential and small commercial customers are eligible to pair grid-parallel storage with solar and take service under Phase One NEM - i.e. adding a battery does not by itself force a move off Phase One NEM. Storage may only be added to a Phase One NEM system if it is paired with another Phase One NEM-eligible technology. Adding an ESS to an existing DG facility is filed as a Battery Energy Storage application with SIR Appendix K; a new PV plus new storage project is filed as a single Hybrid application. Metering: three acceptable hybrid configurations - exclusive ESS charge from PV, PV export only, and separate metering; the PSC approved a three-meter configuration for hybrid ESS in Case 18-E-0081, Order Modifying Standardized Interconnection Requirements issued 2018-04-19. Technologies behind one meter that are credited under different rate structures require specialized metering and/or relaying. NOTE: this guide is Version 4, July 2022, aligned to the May 2022 SIR - re-verify against the 2026-02-09 SIR.

programs.limits: Season May 1-Sep 30; availability window 12pm-7pm; event duration up to 4 hours; up to 20 events per season
programs.export: Net export during events is credited in the performance calculation; NEM/VDER customers are eligible
programs.stack: NYSERDA Residential Energy Storage Incentive (enrollment required for applications on/after 3/1/2026); NEM/VDER

programs.struct: $/kW-month reservation payment + $/kWh performance payment (or voluntary $/kWh only)
programs.val: Reservation Payment Option: $4.25/kW-month in months with 4 or fewer planned events, $4.50/kW-month in months with 5 or more planned events; performance $0.50/kWh. Voluntary Participation Option: $0.50/kWh performance only
programs.limits: Capability period May 1-Sep 30; weekdays only; events begin at 2 p.m. and require at least 4 hours of reduction; Reservation option may require a 1-hour test event; performance factor above 25% required to earn reservation payments; enroll by Apr 1 (May 1 start) or May 1 (Jun 1 start); Voluntary enrollment open through Sep 30
programs.peak: Events begin 2:00pm weekdays May-Sep; minimum 4-hour duration
programs.stack: Distribution Load Relief Program (DLRP); Term-DLM/Auto-DLM; NYISO DR programs

programs.struct: $/kW-month reservation payment + $/kWh performance payment; reservation rate currently set to zero
programs.val: Reservation payment level set at $0.00 per kW-month; the company reported it intends to hold the DLRP incentive at $0.00/kW-month indefinitely until a distribution need arises, and there were no 2025 enrollments
programs.limits: Tariff program remains on the books but is effectively dormant while the reservation rate is $0.00
programs.stack: Commercial System Relief Program (CSRP); NYISO DR programs

programs.struct: contract demand $/kW-month + as-used daily demand charges
programs.limits: Applies to customers with on-site generation or storage; RG&E may exempt up to 150 non-NEM-eligible customers from standby rates under the PSC standby-rate exemption framework; rate detail is in the RG&E electric tariff leaves and is not published on the customer-facing site
programs.tariff: Service Classification No. 14 - Standby Delivery Service (RG&E PSC No. 19 - Electricity)

programs.struct: upfront enrollment gift card + end-of-season bill credit
programs.val: $70 e-gift card on enrollment plus a $20 bill credit at the end of the season for participating in temperature adjustments (requires participating in at least one full event)
programs.limits: Season May 1-Sep 30 on the highest summer demand days, excluding holidays; events typically last 1-4 hours; participation is voluntary and a customer can opt out of any adjustment at the thermostat; requires an eligible connected smart thermostat controlling central air conditioning
programs.peak: Event window May 1-Sep 30 on peak summer days
programs.stack: Energy Storage Solutions Program (BYOB); Time-of-Use service class (SC-4)

programs.struct: two-period TOU supply price with a flat delivery charge across all hours
programs.limits: Peak hours are Monday-Friday 7am-9pm; all remaining hours are off-peak; customers using 24,750 kWh or less per year are placed on TOU Schedule I and customers above 24,750 kWh per year on TOU Schedule II; the delivery charge is the same in all hours so the TOU differential is in the supply price
programs.tariff: Service Classification No. 4 - Residential Time-of-Use (RG&E PSC No. 19 - Electricity)
programs.peak: Peak Mon-Fri 7am-9pm; off-peak all remaining hours
programs.stack: Energy Storage Solutions Program (BYOB); Value Stack / net metering

programs.struct: hourly energy price indexed to the NYISO day-ahead LBMP
programs.limits: Mandatory hourly pricing applies to larger demand-billed commercial and industrial accounts; price is derived from the day-ahead NYISO Locational Based Marginal Price for the customer's region, weighted by service-classification load profile for the calendar month and day type
programs.peak: Hourly - price varies every hour of every day
programs.rates: Hourly day-ahead NYISO LBMP plus applicable delivery and adjustment charges
programs.stack: Commercial System Relief Program (CSRP); Value Stack (VDER)

programs.struct: one-time enrollment incentive + monthly off-peak charging rewards paid quarterly
programs.val: $25 one-time enrollment incentive for activating the charger; monthly rewards are earned when 80% or more of total home EV charging occurs off-peak and increase with additional off-peak charging; the per-kWh reward value is not published on the program page
programs.limits: Requires an EV owned or leased by the customer and a Level 2 home charger; accumulated monthly rewards are paid quarterly in the month following the quarter end
programs.stack: Time-of-Use service class (SC-4); Smart Savings Rewards

programs.struct: competitive-bid $/kW capacity payment capped by a published Incentive Rate
programs.val: Incentive Rate that caps maximum annual per-kW compensation was $26.25/kW in the January 2025 RFP (up from $25.50/kW in the December 2023 RFP); actual payment is set by accepted bid
programs.limits: Bids provide Load Relief in fixed 4-hour Call Windows on weekdays with at least 21 hours notice; minimum bid 50 kW of Cleared Quantity per aggregation per program and vintage year; proposed Load Relief amounts and locations must stay the same for each contract year
programs.peak: Fixed 4-hour weekday call windows during the capability period

programs.struct: competitive-bid $/kW capacity payment capped by a published Incentive Rate
programs.val: Incentive Rate that caps maximum annual per-kW compensation was $26.25/kW in the January 2025 RFP (up from $25.50/kW in the December 2023 RFP); actual payment is set by accepted bid
programs.limits: Bids provide Load Relief with at least 10 minutes notice, up to 18 hours per day, 7 days a week; minimum bid 50 kW of Cleared Quantity per aggregation per program and vintage year; proposed Load Relief amounts and locations must stay the same for each contract year
programs.peak: Up to 18 hours per day, 7 days a week, with 10 minutes notice

ic.rule_summary: Follows the statewide SIR with no separate interconnection procedure of its own (only a utility-specific technical requirements document for inverter settings). Deviation is the utility-specific monthly Customer Benefit Contribution rate charged to mass-market and small-commercial BTM generation interconnected on or after 2022-01-01. 2026 CBC: net-metered PV $1.31/kW-month residential and $0.96/kW-month small commercial; Value Stack PV $0.65 and $0.67.
ic.storage_specific_notes: No utility-specific storage deviation identified. State SIR Sec I.E and Appendix K govern; adding an ESS to an existing DG facility is filed with Appendix K at any time.

programs.n: Value Stack (Value of Distributed Energy Resources / VDER) Tariff
programs.struct: component-based export credit ($/kWh + $/kW) applied as monetary bill credits
programs.val: $0.84/kW-mo residential and $1.28/kW-mo small commercial CBC (2026, Value Stack PV)
programs.limits: Phase Two eligibility: on-site DG >750 kW plus remote net metered and community DG of any size; CHP excluded. Phase One (pre-7/26/2018 qualifiers) uses $/kW-yr DRV/LSRV and a Market Transition Credit
programs.peak: DRV: assigned 4-hour window on summer non-holiday weekdays Jun 24-Sep 15; ICAP Alt 2: 2pm-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31
programs.export: Value Stack credit = LBMP (day-ahead energy) + ICAP capacity (Alt 1 all-hours $/kWh, Alt 2 concentrated 240-245 summer afternoon hrs 2-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31, or Alt 3 $/kW-month coincident-peak - Alt 3 required for dispatchable/paired storage) + Environmental (REC or social cost of carbon $/kWh) + DRV ($/kWh on export in an assigned 4-hr summer weekday window Jun 24-Sep 15) + LSRV ($/kW-event in designated high-value areas until MW cap) + Community Credit for CDG. Values vary hourly and by utility/zone - see utility Value Stack calculator
programs.stack: NY-Sun; NYSERDA Retail Energy Storage Incentive; utility DR programs

programs.n: Phase One Net Energy Metering (mass market) with Customer Benefit Contribution
programs.struct: 1:1 kWh net metering credit plus a monthly $/kW-DC Customer Benefit Contribution charge
programs.val: $1.67/kW-mo residential and $1.83/kW-mo small commercial CBC (2026)
programs.limits: Available to residential and small commercial (non-demand-billed) PV; CBC applies to systems interconnected on or after 1/1/2022 and is recalculated annually; pre-2022 systems exempt; CBC cannot be netted against production
programs.tariff: Net Energy Metering / Customer Benefit Contribution (PSC Case 15-E-0751)
programs.export: 1:1 retail-rate kWh net metering (mass market PV); monthly CBC charge assessed on DC system size
programs.stack: NY-Sun; NYSERDA Retail Energy Storage Incentive

programs.n: Bring Your Own Battery (BYOB) residential direct load control
programs.struct: annual $/kW-yr performance payment (design follows Joint Utilities BYOB template)
programs.limits: PSC-directed residential storage direct load control program; NYSERDA reported launch expected later in 2026

programs.struct: $/kW-month reservation payment + $/kWh performance payment (or voluntary $/kWh only)
programs.val: Reservation Payment Option: $1.23/kW-month, rising to $1.54/kW-month from the month of the 5th event through September if 5 or more events are called; performance $0.11/kWh planned events and $0.21/kWh unplanned events. Voluntary Payment Option: no reservation payment, $0.11/kWh planned and $0.35/kWh unplanned
programs.limits: Capability period Jun 1-Sep 30; events Monday-Friday between 12:00am and 8:00pm; at least 21 hours notice for planned events; reduction sustained up to 4 hours; Reservation option requires one 1-hour test event per year on a non-holiday weekday; communicating interval meter required; TDR participants are not eligible for CSRP
programs.tariff: CSRP tariff (Central Hudson PSC No. 15 - Electricity)
programs.stack: NYISO DR programs; not stackable with Targeted Demand Response (TDR)

programs.struct: $/kW-month payment for committed load reduction in constrained areas
programs.val: $6.82 per kW of load reduction per month of participation (June through September)
programs.limits: Available only to commercial and industrial customers located in specific energy-constrained program areas; interval metering required; TDR participants may not also participate in CSRP
programs.tariff: Targeted Demand Response (Central Hudson Peak Perks)
programs.stack: NYISO DR programs; not stackable with CSRP

programs.n: Peak Perks My Thermostat Rewards (Bring Your Own Thermostat)
programs.struct: upfront enrollment reward + annual participation reward
programs.val: $100 enrollment reward per eligible smart thermostat plus a $50 annual reward credited to the account for full summer season participation
programs.limits: Open to Central Hudson residential customers, with priority in targeted areas with distribution constraints; participants must remain enrolled 12 months or part of the enrollment reward is reversed; during a conservation event the compressor runs about half the time it ran in the hour before the event; two opt-outs allowed per program season
programs.tariff: Peak Perks (Central Hudson residential demand response)
programs.stack: Peak Perks Custom Savings; net metering / Value Stack

programs.n: Electric Vehicle Whole Home Time of Use Rate
programs.struct: two-period whole-home TOU rate with first-year bill protection
programs.limits: Optional billing method for residential customers who own an electric vehicle; whole-home usage is billed on the TOU rate, not just the charger; approximately 83% of usage must be shifted off-peak to save versus standard rates; first-year bill protection compares annual usage against standard rates and refunds the difference by check if standard would have been cheaper
programs.tariff: Electric Vehicle Whole Home Time of Use Rate (Central Hudson PSC No. 15 - Electricity)
programs.peak: On-peak Mon-Fri 2:00pm-7:00pm; all weekends and six major holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas) are off-peak
programs.stack: Peak Perks; Value Stack / net metering

programs.struct: two-period TOU rate with a customer-selected on-peak window
programs.limits: Applies only to customers enrolled before Dec 1 2017; not accepting new applications; participants chose one of three weekday on-peak windows: 8am-8pm, 9am-9pm, or 10am-10pm; all weekends and six major holidays are off-peak; new enrollees are directed to the current Time-of-Use Service offering effective Dec 1 2017
programs.tariff: Legacy Time-of-Use Billing (Central Hudson PSC No. 15 - Electricity)
programs.peak: Customer-selected weekday on-peak window of 8am-8pm, 9am-9pm or 10am-10pm; weekends and six major holidays off-peak
programs.stack: Peak Perks; Value Stack / net metering

programs.n: Time-of-Use Service (customers enrolled Dec 1 2017 or after)
programs.struct: two-period TOU rate for customers enrolling on or after Dec 1 2017
programs.limits: Current voluntary TOU offering replacing Legacy Time-of-Use Billing; enrollment is by application form; weekends and six major holidays are off-peak
programs.tariff: Time-of-Use Service (Central Hudson PSC No. 15 - Electricity)
programs.stack: Peak Perks; Value Stack / net metering

programs.struct: sign-on reward + $/kW peak-time rebate on measured event-hour reduction
programs.val: $25 sign-on reward plus $50 per kW saved during conservation events relative to the customer's average usage in those hours
programs.limits: Open to selected customers in specific energy-constrained areas; events called June 1 through September 30 between noon and 8 p.m.
programs.stack: Peak Perks My Thermostat Rewards; Value Stack / net metering

programs.n: EV ChargeSmart Residential Managed Charging Program
programs.struct: enrollment bonus + quarterly $/kWh off-peak charging incentive
programs.val: $25 bonus after three months of successful participation; quarterly participation incentive equal to total off-peak charging kWh times the Savings Rate, which was $0.04/kWh as of Feb 1 2026
programs.limits: Year-round incentives for charging after 7 p.m. and before 2 p.m.; the Savings Rate is recalculated as the sum of the difference between the flat standard residential delivery rate and the off-peak residential TOU delivery rate plus the difference between standard flat supply charges and off-peak supply charges
programs.peak: Off-peak charging after 7:00pm and before 2:00pm, year-round
programs.rates: Off-peak charging incentive $0.04/kWh (Savings Rate effective Feb 1 2026)
programs.stack: Electric Vehicle Whole Home Time of Use Rate; Peak Perks

programs.struct: contract demand $/kW-month + as-used daily demand charges
programs.limits: New standby rates under Service Classification No. 14 took effect January 1 2024; standby rates may be required for customers with on-site generation who do not qualify for net metering or the Value Stack; customers on standby rates must have interval metering recording at 15-minute to 1-hour intervals; rate detail appears at leaf 272 of the Central Hudson electric tariff; Central Hudson may exempt up to 100 non-NEM-eligible customers from standby rates
programs.tariff: Service Classification No. 14 - Standby Service (Central Hudson PSC No. 15 - Electricity)
programs.export: Customers taking standby service generally take Value Stack rather than net metering

ic.rule_summary: Follows the statewide SIR with no separate interconnection procedure of its own (only a utility-specific technical requirements document for inverter settings). Deviation is the utility-specific monthly Customer Benefit Contribution rate charged to mass-market and small-commercial BTM generation interconnected on or after 2022-01-01. 2026 CBC: net-metered PV $1.67/kW-month residential and $1.83/kW-month small commercial (the highest in the state); Value Stack PV $0.84 and $1.28.
ic.storage_specific_notes: No utility-specific storage deviation identified. State SIR Sec I.E and Appendix K govern; adding an ESS to an existing DG facility is filed with Appendix K at any time.

LONG ISLAND POWER AUTHORITY.name: Long Island Power Authority / PSEG Long Island

programs.n: Net Energy Metering with Customer Benefit Contribution (mass market)
programs.struct: 1:1 kWh net metering credit plus monthly $/kW-DC Customer Benefit Contribution charge
programs.val: $1.13/kW-mo residential and $1.19/kW-mo small commercial CBC (2026)
programs.limits: Mass-market LIPA projects cannot opt into the Value Stack (VDER); Value Stack is available to larger and CDG projects under the LIPA tariff
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - Net Metering / CBC
programs.export: 1:1 retail net metering for mass market PV; monthly CBC charge on DC system size; VDER Value Stack not available to mass market
programs.stack: NY-Sun; NYSERDA Retail Energy Storage Incentive

programs.struct: component-based export credit (LBMP + ICAP + Environmental + DRV + LSRV)
programs.limits: LIPA tariff aligned with PSC VDER orders effective Aug 1 2019; mass-market customers are NOT eligible; CDG projects qualifying before 1/1/2020 receive volumetric rather than monetary crediting for mass-market satellites
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - Value Stack
programs.export: Value Stack credit = LBMP (day-ahead energy) + ICAP capacity (Alt 1 all-hours $/kWh, Alt 2 concentrated 240-245 summer afternoon hrs 2-7pm Jun 24-Aug 31, or Alt 3 $/kW-month coincident-peak - Alt 3 required for dispatchable/paired storage) + Environmental (REC or social cost of carbon $/kWh) + DRV ($/kWh on export in an assigned 4-hr summer weekday window Jun 24-Sep 15) + LSRV ($/kW-event in designated high-value areas until MW cap) + Community Credit for CDG. Values vary hourly and by utility/zone - see utility Value Stack calculator
programs.stack: NY-Sun; NYSERDA Retail Energy Storage Incentive

programs.n: System Peak Relief Program (Commercial System Relief Program / Distribution Load Relief Program)
programs.struct: $/kW reservation payment + $/kWh performance payment; rates derived from PSEG Long Island Marginal Cost of Service (MCOS) Study
programs.limits: Program period May 1-Sep 30; aggregators notified at least 21 hours ahead and again 2 hours before the event; typical event about 4 hours; direct enrollment requires a minimum 50 kW pledge, otherwise enroll through an approved aggregator; AMI meter provided at no cost; existing on-site generation may be used if it complies with the CSRP tariff
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - System Peak Relief (CSRP/DLRP)
programs.peak: Events called May 1-Sep 30 on forecast peak days
programs.stack: Battery Storage Rewards; NYISO DR programs

programs.struct: upfront enrollment incentive + annual retention incentive
programs.val: $85 for installing/enrolling a qualifying smart thermostat plus $25 in each following year of participation
programs.limits: Events called on forecast peak summer days; enrolled homes are pre-cooled 3 degrees for 30 minutes then thermostat setpoint raised 4 degrees during the peak period; customers may opt out of any individual adjustment from thermostat app or device; requires central air conditioning and an approved internet-connected thermostat

programs.struct: annual performance payment paid through a third-party aggregator; payment terms set by the aggregator
programs.limits: Event season May 1-Sep 30; fewer than 10 events per summer; each event a maximum of 4 hours; aggregators notified a day ahead with at least 21 hours notice; enrollment only through an approved aggregator, which remotely discharges the battery; opting out of an event reduces payment
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - Battery Storage Rewards
programs.peak: Event window May 1-Sep 30 on forecast near-peak days
programs.stack: NY-Sun / NYSERDA Long Island storage incentive; net metering

programs.n: Time-of-Day Off-Peak Rate (standard residential TOD rate)
programs.struct: seasonal two-period time-of-day rate replacing the Rate 180 flat rate
programs.limits: Peak hours are weekdays 3:00pm-7:00pm; all other hours are off-peak; nights, weekends and federal holidays are always off-peak; rates differ between summer and non-summer seasons; PSEG Long Island began migrating residential accounts off the Rate 180 flat rate to this TOD rate in 2024 (with exceptions); Guaranteed Bill Protection closed to new enrollees, customers starting service, or customers voluntarily selecting a TOD rate as of January 2026, but continues up to 12 months for accounts that started a TOD rate before January 2026
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - Time-of-Day Off-Peak Rate
programs.peak: Peak weekdays 3:00pm-7:00pm; all other hours off-peak; nights weekends and federal holidays always off-peak
programs.stack: Battery Storage Rewards; Smart Savers; net metering / TOD Net Meter Bank Exchange

programs.struct: time-of-day rate with a deeply discounted overnight super-off-peak period
programs.val: Overnight hours discounted up to 40% off the Rate 180 flat rate
programs.limits: Voluntary alternative to the standard Time-of-Day Off-Peak Rate; peak hours weekdays 3:00pm-7:00pm; designed for customers who can shift large loads such as EV charging to overnight hours
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - Super Off-Peak Rate
programs.peak: Peak weekdays 3:00pm-7:00pm; discounted overnight super-off-peak window
programs.rates: Overnight super-off-peak discounted up to 40% versus the Rate 180 flat rate
programs.stack: Battery Storage Rewards; Smart Savers; net metering

programs.n: Time of Day Net Meter Bank Exchange
programs.struct: transfer of banked net-metering kWh credits between peak and off-peak credit banks
programs.limits: Applies to customers who began net metering in 2018 or later and are billed on a Time-of-Day rate (rate 194 or 195); excess generation accrues in separate peak and off-peak energy banks; one transfer per bill cycle may be requested using the Excess Generation Exchange Authorization Form and is applied to the next bill
programs.tariff: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service - Time of Day Net Metering
programs.peak: Peak weekdays 3:00pm-7:00pm; all other hours off-peak
programs.export: Net metering credits bank separately by TOD period; customers may move off-peak credits to offset peak usage one time per bill cycle
programs.stack: Time-of-Day Off-Peak Rate; Super Off-Peak Rate; Battery Storage Rewards

programs.struct: monthly service charge + contract demand $/kW + as-used daily demand charges with a 3-period time-of-use structure
programs.limits: Effective January 1 2026; replaces the former SC 12 Back-Up and Supplemental Service and closed Rate Code 681. Commercial standby is Rate Code 682 with eleven sub-rate codes; optional residential standby rates are also offered. Mandatory for about 72 existing commercial customers, optional for most others (SC-5, SC-7, SC-10, SC-13, unmetered and non-AMI customers may not opt in). Existing mandatory customers default to a five-year phase-in running Jan 1 2026 through Dec 31 2030, with full standby rates for everyone on Jan 1 2031; new customers taking service after the amendment date pay full standby rates with no phase-in. Optional Rate Customers must have an AMI meter and, if they switch back to a flat non-time-varying rate, cannot return to standby or another time-varying rate for at least one year. Standby customers qualifying for Rate 285-Primary or Rate 285-Transmission who take Authority supply are billed supply hourly at LBMP plus capacity based on their individual capacity tag. Peak-to-off-peak as-used daily demand ratio is 1.25:1, producing a summer-to-winter demand rate ratio of 2.25; the Super Off-Peak period incurs no as-used daily demand charge
programs.tariff: Service Classification No. 12 - Standby Service (LIPA Tariff for Electric Service); Rate Code 682
programs.peak: Summer (Jun-Sep): Peak 3pm-7pm M-F excluding federal holidays; Off-Peak 8am-3pm and 7pm-10pm M-F plus 8am-10pm weekends and federal holidays; Super Off-Peak 10pm-8am every day. Winter (Oct-May): no Peak period, Off-Peak 8am-10pm every day, Super Off-Peak 10pm-8am every day
programs.rates: As-used daily demand charged in Peak and Off-Peak periods only; Super Off-Peak (10pm-8am) has no as-used daily demand charge
programs.stack: Buyback Service (SC 11); Battery Storage Rewards; System Peak Relief Program

programs.struct: customer charge + buyback contract demand charge on injections, set equal to the applicable Standby Service rates
programs.limits: Updated effective January 1 2026 alongside the new Standby Service rates. Buyback Service applies to customers with on-site generation exporting power to the Authority. The tariff adds a Customer Charge and a Buyback Contract Demand Charge on the customer's injections, with Customer and Contract Demand rates set equal to those of the applicable Standby Service rate for the customer's requirements from the system. Consistent with the PSC Allocated Cost of Service Order, stand-alone Energy Storage Systems that reach Step 3 of the Small Generator Interconnection Procedures before December 31 2030 are exempt from Buyback Contract Demand Charges for 15 years from the project's in-service date. Buyback rates remain under Rate Code 289
programs.tariff: Service Classification No. 11 - Buyback Service (LIPA Tariff for Electric Service); Rate Code 289
programs.export: Export from on-site generation is compensated under Buyback Service; a Buyback Contract Demand Charge now applies to injections, with a 15-year exemption for stand-alone storage reaching SGIP Step 3 before Dec 31 2030
programs.stack: Standby Service (SC 12); Value Stack (VDER); Battery Storage Rewards

programs.struct: upfront rebate on a qualifying Level 2 EV charger
programs.val: $100 rebate for a qualified Level 2 charger from the EPRI Vetted Product List; customers in Disadvantaged Communities or on the Household Assistance Program receive an additional $300 for a total of $400
programs.limits: Charger must appear on the EPRI Vetted Product List filtered to PSEG-Long Island; program open with an expected end date of December 31 2026
programs.stack: Time-of-Day Off-Peak Rate; Super Off-Peak Rate

ic.utility_name: Long Island Power Authority / PSEG Long Island
ic.rule_summary: Does NOT follow the New York State SIR. LIPA is a state authority outside PSC jurisdiction and PSL 66-j/66-l do not apply to it. Interconnection runs under LIPA's own Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGIP), an addendum to LIPA's Tariff for Electric Service, administered by PSEG Long Island as LIPA's agent, with a separate Smart Grid SGIP (SGSGIP) track. Scope is broader than the state SIR: distributed generation facilities with a nameplate rating of 10 MW or less aggregated on the customer side of the point of common coupling, versus 5 MW under the PSC SIR. Applications go through PSEG Long Island's Interconnection Online Application Portal (live since 2021-02-12). Separate PSEG Long Island technical requirements documents cover DER up to 500 kVA and above 500 kVA.
ic.ic_application_fee: SGIP application fee $750 for 50 kW to 5 MW and $750 for 5 MW to 10 MW, payable to PSEG Long Island (SGIP Application Instructions, https://www.psegliny.com/aboutpseglongisland/ratesandtariffs/sgip/applications). Fee for systems under 50 kW not verified.
ic.external_disconnect: Not verified
ic.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - LIPA SGIP and tariff not verified on whether a battery may charge from the grid and still export or earn credit
ic.standby_charge: Not verified
ic.storage_specific_notes: Not verified. LIPA's storage-specific interconnection and compensation provisions, and whether adding storage to an existing LIPA net-metered system changes compensation, were not established in this pass.

NEW YORK STATE ENERGY RESEARCH AND DEVEL.name: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) - statewide

programs.struct: upfront fixed $/kWh incentive paid through participating contractor; declining MWh block structure by region
programs.limits: Up to 25 kWh of storage capacity per home; first-come first-served; block rates vary by region (NYC, Westchester, Rest of State, Long Island) and decline as blocks fill; from 3/1/2026 projects in National Grid, NYSEG and RG&E territory must also enroll in the utility BYOB program (other utilities on rolling dates)
programs.stack: Utility Bring Your Own Battery programs; NY-Sun; VDER Value Stack

programs.struct: upfront fixed $/kWh incentive; declining MWh block structure by region
programs.limits: New commercial-scale distributed storage up to 5 MW, behind the meter or interconnected to the distribution network; project must provide customer value under an IOU rate (demand-charge offset, utility DR participation, or VDER compensation); block rates vary by region and decline as blocks fill
programs.stack: Utility DR programs; VDER Value Stack; NYSERDA Bulk Storage (>5 MW)

programs.struct: enriched upfront $/kWh incentive for disadvantaged-community or income-eligible households
programs.val: $450/kWh for Block 1 ($11.25M for a 10 MW / 25 MWh statewide block)
programs.limits: Must meet all market-rate Residential Storage Incentive requirements plus one of: site in a Climate Justice Working Group DAC census tract; owner-occupied household under 80% AMI or SMI; or 1-4 unit affordable housing. 80 MW of the 200 MW residential program allocated to ISI. Long Island (LIPA/PSEG) NOT included
programs.stack: Utility Bring Your Own Battery programs; NY-Sun

programs.struct: enriched upfront $/kWh incentive for DAC-sited critical facilities and affordable housing
programs.val: $350/kWh for Block 1 ($15.75M for a 15 MW / 45 MWh statewide block)
programs.limits: Must meet all market-rate Retail Storage Incentive requirements plus all of: sited in a DAC census tract; behind-the-meter and configured for backup power during outages; at an eligible public/nonprofit critical facility or affordable housing. Minimum 60 MW allocated. CDG and remote-crediting projects ineligible. Long Island (LIPA/PSEG) NOT included
programs.stack: Utility DR programs; VDER Value Stack

programs.n: Long Island Single-Family Residential Storage Incentive
programs.struct: upfront $/kWh incentive administered under the NY-Sun Program Manual
programs.limits: Applies to residential storage installed in PSEG Long Island territory; administered separately from the statewide Residential Storage Incentive and governed by the NY-Sun Program Manual; not eligible for the statewide Inclusive Storage Incentive blocks
programs.stack: NY-Sun; PSEG Long Island DR programs

programs.struct: upfront $/W declining megawatt-block incentive paid through participating contractor
programs.limits: Block incentive levels ($/W) vary by region (Con Edison, Upstate, Long Island) and by sector, and decline as each megawatt block fills; adders exist for affordable housing and low-to-moderate-income customers
programs.stack: NYSERDA Residential/Retail Storage Incentive; VDER Value Stack; net metering

programs.n: Net Billing Tariff (NBT) - successor to net energy metering; IOUs brand it 'Solar Billing Plan'
programs.struct: Hourly avoided-cost export credit (Avoided Cost Calculator values) + 9-yr ACC Plus adder for PG&E/SCE residential
programs.limits: Applies to interconnection applications submitted on/after 2023-04-15; 9-year NBT legacy period for the original interconnecting customer; system sizing up to annual load +50% with attestation
programs.tariff: CPUC D.22-12-056 (adopted 2022-12-15); implemented via Resolution E-5301 (2023-11-30)
programs.peak: n/a - export credit is hourly, 8760 values per utility
programs.rates: Import billed on a required 'electrification' TOU rate: E-ELEC (PG&E), TOU-D-PRIME (SCE), EV-TOU-5 (SDG&E)
programs.export: Exports credited at CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator hourly values (usually below retail; can exceed retail on late-summer evenings); net surplus at true-up paid at wholesale (~$0.02-0.03/kWh)

programs.struct: Retail-rate bill credit for exports (import rates), netted per metered interval
programs.limits: Closed to applications after 2023-04-14. 20-year legacy period from interconnection date (D.14-03-041); legacy runs with the system, not the owner. NEM 1.0 customers who rolled to NEM 2.0 do not get a second 20 years
programs.rates: Exports credited at the customer's retail import rate
programs.export: 1:1 retail-rate net metering, netted hourly (residential) / 15-min (non-res); non-bypassable charges on each net kWh consumed; net surplus at wholesale (~$0.02-0.03/kWh)
programs.stack: Storage may be paired with a NEM 2.0 system under D.14-05-033 / D.16-04-020 metering rules without losing legacy status

programs.n: NEM legacy forfeiture threshold for system modifications (storage additions)
programs.struct: Rule, not an incentive
programs.limits: A grandfathered NEM 1.0/2.0 customer moves to the Solar Billing Plan at their next True-Up only if they increase the RENEWABLE GENERATING nameplate capacity by more than the greater of 1 kW or 10% of the original facility. Adding battery storage alone does not increase renewable generating nameplate capacity and therefore does not forfeit NEM legacy status. PG&E states this in its Solar Billing Plan FAQ.
programs.export: Adding storage to a grandfathered NEM 2.0 system preserves NEM 2.0 export compensation; adding PV capacity above the 1 kW / 10% threshold forfeits it

programs.n: Emergency Load Reduction Program (ELRP) - non-residential / Group A and Group B
programs.struct: $/kWh performance payment for measured load reduction; no penalty for non-performance
programs.val: $2.00/kWh for every kWh of measured voluntary reduction (non-residential)
programs.limits: May-Oct, 7 days/wk, 4-9pm window; events 1 hr min to 5 hr max; up to 60 event-hours per year; consecutive days allowed. Triggered by CAISO EEA Watch/EEA-1/2/3 or (residential) a day-ahead Flex Alert
programs.tariff: ELRP pilot per CPUC D.21-12-015 as updated by D.23-12-005
programs.rates: n/a - event-based payment, not a rate
programs.export: BTM solar+storage with permission to export explicitly eligible under Group A
programs.stack: Group B allows customers already in CAISO market-integrated DR (DRAM, CBP) to earn ELRP for INCREMENTAL reduction beyond what is committed to CAISO. Base Interruptible Program customers are eligible for Group A

programs.n: Power Saver Rewards (residential ELRP sub-program A.6)
programs.struct: $/kWh performance payment for incremental load reduction during events
programs.val: $1.00/kWh for voluntary incremental residential load reduction
programs.limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm; 1-5 hr events; 60 hr/yr program cap. Nearly 4 million IOU customers were auto-enrolled starting summer 2022
programs.export: n/a - measured against a baseline, not an export tariff

programs.n: Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) - Residential Solar and Storage Equity (RSSE, AB 209 budget)
programs.struct: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate + $/kW solar rebate
programs.val: Storage $1,100/kWh; Solar $3,100/kW (CPUC-published rate table, current as of 2026-09-16). Authorized budget $280 million
programs.limits: Reservations opened 2025-06-02. Open to any low-income residential electric and/or gas customer in California (not only IOU customers). All applicants must enroll in a qualified Demand Response program within one year of reserving funds. CPUC D.24-03-071 established the budget; Resolution E-5362 opened it; Resolution E-5373 handles IRA tax-credit interaction
programs.export: Rebate is upfront; export compensation comes from the customer's NEM/NBT tariff
programs.stack: NBT / Solar Billing Plan; ELRP; a qualified DR program is REQUIRED

programs.n: SGIP - Small Residential Storage budget (general market)
programs.struct: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
programs.val: $150/kWh (CPUC rate table)
programs.limits: CPUC lists this budget as available through 2025. Requires enrollment in a qualified DR program within one year of reservation

programs.struct: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
programs.val: $1,000/kWh (CPUC rate table)
programs.limits: CPUC lists this budget as available through 2025. Targeted at customers in high fire-threat districts, PSPS-affected areas and medical-baseline / vulnerable households. Established by D.19-09-027

programs.n: SGIP - San Joaquin Valley Residential budget
programs.struct: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
programs.val: $1,100/kWh (CPUC rate table)
programs.limits: PG&E or SCE residential customers only; CPUC lists as available through 2025

programs.n: SGIP - Non-Residential Equity and Large-Scale Storage budgets
programs.struct: Upfront $/kWh storage rebate
programs.val: Non-Residential Equity $850/kWh; Large-Scale Storage $250/kWh; SCE San Joaquin Valley Non-Residential $1,000/kWh; Generation $2,000/kW (CPUC rate table)
programs.limits: IOU customers (PG&E, SCE, SDG&E, SoCalGas) including unbundled/CCA customers. CPUC lists these budgets as available through 2025
programs.stack: ELRP; Base Interruptible Program; Capacity Bidding Program

programs.struct: Upfront capacity commitment payment plus per-unit net-load-reduction payment
programs.limits: Events May through October during extreme grid events. Options 1-4; residential batteries participate via aggregators. Guidelines Fifth Edition adopted 2026; CEC issued a budget update notice 2025-10-01
programs.rates: n/a - event payment, not a rate
programs.export: n/a
programs.stack: Separate from and stackable in principle with CPUC ELRP; verify per-event double-counting rules with the administrator (Olivine)

programs.struct: Competitive auction for Resource Adequacy capacity from third-party DR aggregators bidding into CAISO
programs.limits: Last delivery year was 2024. The CPUC issued its final decision in April 2024 to discontinue DRAM after the 2024 delivery year; the pilot ran from 2016 through 2024 via D.16-06-029, D.17-10-017 and D.19-07-009. Successor capacity-accreditation treatment for DR is being developed in the CPUC DR proceeding
programs.tariff: DRAM pilot (CPUC DR proceeding; CAISO Proxy Demand Resource registration)
programs.stack: Superseded; aggregators now reach CAISO via the Proxy Demand Resource / DERP models and ELRP

programs.struct: Hourly Energy Export Credit at ACC values, plus Energy Export Bonus Credit (ACC Plus adder) for residential systems receiving PTO before 2028
programs.limits: Residential Energy Export Bonus Credit locked at PTO and paid for 9 years; available only to customers on the Solar Billing Plan before 2028. Business customers moved to SBP billing March 2026
programs.peak: Required import rate: E-ELEC (Electric Home), peak 4-9 p.m. daily
programs.export: Hourly Energy Export Credit set from CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator; 8760 hourly values published per year (2023-2026 sheets posted); + ACC Plus adder for residential pre-2028 adopters

programs.n: Schedule E-TOU-C - Residential Time-of-Use (Peak Pricing 4-9 p.m. Every Day)

programs.limits: Bill protection closed to customers enrolling after 2022-05-04

programs.n: Schedule EV2 (EV2-A) - Residential Time-of-Use for Plug-in Electric Vehicle Customers

programs.rates: Total bundled eff 2026-06-01: summer peak $0.53809 / part-peak $0.42760 / off-peak $0.22558; winter peak $0.41099 / part-peak $0.39428 / off-peak $0.22558 per kWh

programs.n: Emergency Load Reduction Program (PG&E, administered via Olivine)
programs.struct: $/kWh performance payment

programs.limits: May-Oct, 4-9pm, 1-5 hr events, 60 hr/yr cap

programs.struct: $/kW-month capacity payment on Potential Load Reduction, with $/kWh penalty for energy above Firm Service Level
programs.val: 15-Minute BIP: Nov-Apr $10.60 (1-500 kW) / $11.20 (501-1,000 kW) / $11.80 (>1,000 kW) per kW-month; May-Oct $13.60 / $14.20 / $14.80 per kW-month. 30-Minute BIP: Nov-Apr $9.50 / $10.00 / $10.50; May-Oct $12.50 / $13.00 / $13.50 per kW-month. Rates effective 2025-05-17 (Advice 7572-E); D.23-12-005 authorized the $2/kW May-Oct adder for 2024-2027. Excess Energy Charge $6.00/kWh above Firm Service Level ($8.40/kWh after a failed re-test)

Two utility test events per year count as program events. Requires >=100 kW max demand and FSL <=85% of highest monthly max demand, minimum 100 kW reduction

programs.n: Underfrequency Relay (UFR) Program (rider to Schedule E-BIP)

programs.val: $0.67/kW-month demand credit on average monthly summer on-peak / winter partial-peak demand
programs.limits: Automatic interruption when system frequency drops to 59.65 Hz for 20 cycles. Direct-enrolled customers only (not available through DR aggregators). PG&E may require up to 3 years written notice to terminate

'Elect' option: max 1 event/day, 4-hour max event duration, participant may elect more than 6 events/month. Day-ahead notification by 5 p.m. Triggered by a CAISO market award for the CBP PDR. NO minimum demand requirement. Net-metered, partial-standby, Auto-DR, bundled, DA and CCA customers eligible; full-standby, WAPA-served and NEMCCSF customers are not

programs.peak: May 1 - Oct 31 event windows, day-ahead notice

programs.n: Schedule E-OBMC - Optional Binding Mandatory Curtailment Plan

ic.rule_summary: Follows the CPUC NEM 2.0 / Net Billing Tariff and PG&E's own Electric Rule 21. Utility-specific items: NEM/NBT interconnection fee for facilities <=1 MW is $145 (CPUC); required NBT import rate is E-ELEC; residential NBT customers receive the ACC Plus adder (PG&E adder table not independently read). Legacy tariff is Electric Schedule NEM2.
ic.export_credit_value: ACC Plus adder applies to residential NBT (PG&E adder values not read - see state row for SCE values)
ic.ic_application_fee: $145 one-time for NEM/NBT <=1 MW (CPUC NEM/NBT page); >1 MW $800 plus study costs
ic.storage_specific_notes: PG&E Sched. NEM2 SC 8.b (Sheet 32, Advice 7489-E, eff. 2025-01-22) carries the D.22-12-056 / D.24-03-071 storage-retrofit language verbatim. Battery retrofit on legacy NEM 2.0: adding only storage does NOT forfeit the 20-year NEM 2.0 legacy period. Tariff text (Sched. NEM2/NEM-ST legacy provisions, 'Pursuant to D.22-12-056'): the addition of energy storage to the existing Generating Facility shall not disqualify the customer from the remainder of the 20-year Transition Period. EXCEPTION per D.24-03-071: customers who add storage through SGIP and apply and have a reservation accepted on or after 2024-06-04 must transition to the Net Billing Tariff, unless in the SGIP Residential Solar and Storage Equity, low-income Equity Resiliency residential, or San Joaquin Valley Residential budgets. Adding PV beyond the greater of 10% or 1 kW of original nameplate still triggers loss of legacy unless the expansion goes on a Rule 21 Non-Export agreement. Legacy NEM-paired storage stays eligible only if storage capacity is not later increased by more than 10% (SCE NEM-ST SC 6.e). NBT customers adding storage (only) to a storage-less system keep the remainder of their 9-year NBT legacy period. Grid charging: NEM/NBT tariffs define a Directly Connected storage device as one that may be charged from the grid, but exports are credited only for renewable-derived energy - Small paired storage (<=10 kW AC) uses a monthly PV-estimate cap on creditable exports (excess forfeited); Large paired storage (>10 kW AC) needs extra metering (storage treated as non-NEM generator, metering cost capped at $600 unless complex) or certified power-control (no storage export, or no grid charging; open-loop response <=10 s). Large paired storage limited to 150% of renewable max output; D.20-06-017 waiver extended by Executive Director to 2025-08-15 - current status Unclear.

ic.utility_name: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP)
ic.rule_summary: Municipal utility outside CPUC jurisdiction; not bound by Rule 21 or the NBT. Governed by the LADWP NEM Service Rider and NEM Guidelines (rev. 11/23/2020, amended Jan 2021) plus the LADWP Electric Service Requirements (ESR). Export credit is still retail-rate kWh netting (credit applied to later bills except taxes and minimum charges; any credit balance is zeroed with no payout when service terminates). NEM eligible rates: R-1, A-1, A-2, A-3. Systems >1 MW-AC(CEC) go to Parallel Generation Schedule CG-2 or CG-3. Process: online application at the Solar Automated Meter Spot portal for a Work Request number; PV <10 kW-AC without service upgrade or battery backup may be fast-tracked; inspections by LADBS, LADWP Electric Service Representative (>=10 kW and some smaller cases) and LADWP Solar Inspector. Interconnection Agreement required where PV and/or ESS >10 kW-AC: Short-Form IA for >10 to <=30 kW-AC, Long-Form IA with single-line diagram for PV >30 kW-AC. All grid-interconnected Energy Storage Systems require preliminary review and inspection by an LADWP Distribution Engineer and ESR (so storage never gets the PV fast track).
ic.nem_cap_res_kw: 1000 kW-AC (CEC) for NEM; larger systems go to Schedule CG-2/CG-3
ic.export_credit_value: Retail-rate netting (confirmed; values captured elsewhere)
ic.ic_study_trigger_kw: 30 kW-AC - Long-Form IA and Distribution Engineer review above this; any ESS triggers Distribution Engineer/ESR review
ic.external_disconnect: Required - all PV systems must have a disconnect device per the LADWP ESR, readily accessible and located near the billing/performance meter
ic.non_export_option: Yes - ESR requires power controls to prevent inadvertent export where required, with settings adjustable only by the manufacturer or its designated qualified worker, not the customer (Secondary - ESR Sec. 8i as indexed, PDF not rendered)
ic.storage_specific_notes: Per LADWP ESR Sec. 8i (as indexed by search; PDF would not render for direct reading): battery storage may not export to the grid under NEM unless it is exclusively charged by eligible renewable parallel generation - so a grid-charged battery must be controlled as non-export. Battery retrofit: LADWP NEM is still open retail-rate netting with no legacy/successor split, so adding a battery does not change export compensation; the retrofit does require a Distribution Engineer/ESR review and, if the ESS is >10 kW-AC, an Interconnection Agreement. Battery-backup projects are excluded from the <10 kW solar fast track.

ic.rule_summary: Publicly-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction (SMUD Board sets rates). Interconnection under SMUD's own Rule and Regulation 21 and Rate Policy 11-01 Interconnection Guidelines (Feb 2022); interconnected energy storage is treated as distributed generation under Rule 21. Applications via PowerClerk; SMUD may require agreements up to 500 kW and generally requires executed agreements above 500 kW; small-generator distribution process typically <=20 MW. Uses Rule 21 or SMUD Advanced Inverter Function (AIF) settings. Export regime: Rate Schedule SSR (Solar and Storage Rate) mandatory for renewable generation approved on or after 2022-03-01 - residential must be on R-TOD; sized to offset up to 110% of own requirements; max 3,000 kW; all kWh registered on the bi-directional meter as delivered to SMUD credited at the Export Compensation Rate ($0.0960/kWh eff. 2026-06-01, updated every 4 years, max +/-30%); credit offsets only usage charges and carries forward. Legacy NEM1 customers (approved before 2022-03-01) may stay on NEM1 through 2030-12-31.
ic.export_credit_value: SSR $0.0960/kWh flat export rate eff. 2026-06-01 (confirmed; captured elsewhere)
ic.ic_application_fee: Rule 21 Interconnection Fee (Rate Policy 9-02, eff. 2026-06-01, non-refundable, applies to new solar and battery storage incl. storage-only): residential <10 kW $500; residential >=10 to <20 kW $1,000; commercial (and residential >=20 kW) <100 kW $2,500; >=100 to <500 kW $3,350; >=500 kW $5,000 plus cost-based invoice for remaining work incl. telemetry. Prior values $180/$300/$2,000/$2,400. NEM1 customers adding storage are not charged the fee (SMUD FAQ, Secondary).
ic.ic_study_trigger_kw: 500 - executed interconnection agreements generally required above 500 kW; >=500 kW also triggers cost-based billing for remaining interconnection work
ic.non_export_option: Yes - dedicated Non-export interconnection request path in PowerClerk for battery, EV and other DERs not intended to export to the distribution system
ic.standby_threshold_kw: N/A - SSR customers are exempt from generator standby charges on load served by the eligible facility (SSR Sec. III)
ic.storage_specific_notes: Grid charging: SMUD's interconnection page states that to qualify for NEM (NEM1) all storage must be charged with renewable energy on site. Under SSR the tariff defines export as all kWh registered on the bi-directional meter as delivered to SMUD and lets storage-only facilities take SSR, so grid-charged export appears to be credited at the flat SSR rate - this is a reading of the tariff text, not an explicit SMUD statement (flat rate makes arbitrage value low anyway). Battery retrofit on legacy NEM1: SMUD says existing NEM customers can add a battery and stay on NEM1 through 2030-12-31 but are then NOT eligible for My Energy Optimizer Partner+ storage incentives; any customer receiving a SMUD storage incentive must be on SSR (SSR Sec. VIII). Expanding generation by more than the greater of 10% or 1 kW (or beyond 110% of original) forces a move to SSR and a new application. Conflict: the same SMUD FAQ also says customers on NEM who add battery storage will be placed on SSR - read as the incentive path. Storage-only customers cannot be on NEM1. Sizing: SMUD materials (Secondary) allow SSR PV up to 120% of 12-month usage when storage is added; tariff text says 110%.

ic.rule_summary: Irrigation district (publicly owned) outside CPUC jurisdiction; own Electric Service Rule No. 21 and Solar Electric Service Guide. Only NEM 2.0 is offered to new customers: real-time (hourly for residential) netting - imports at MID retail rate, generation exceeding load at that time credited at 7.6 c/kWh as a bill credit. Sizing: PV may not exceed 115% of the meter's annual demonstrated load (CSI calculator); modifications also capped at 115%. Above 1 MW customers pay a capacity charge per kW over the threshold and forfeit excess-generation credits. Application package: MID Solar System & Energy Storage Device Application, Electrical Interconnection Agreement, Net Metering Agreement, single-line diagram, battery data sheet if a battery is installed. MID review up to 30 days; interconnection inspection up to 10 business days; PV+ESS sites need an inspection appointment. MID installs a utility-grade production meter on the AC side of the inverter (customer supplies socket). NEM 1.0 customers who add or rearrange panels increasing output by more than 10% must move to NEM 2.0; NEM 2.0 customers must wait 6 months after interconnection before modifying panels.

ic.external_disconnect: Required - two visible, lockable AC disconnect switches between the PV system and MID's system (one between the panel and production meter socket, within 12 ft and line of sight of the main panel), per MID Solar Electric Service Guide (2019)
ic.non_export_option: Yes - effectively mandatory for storage: MID's Service Guide says all ESS shall be configured for customer backup power or peak shaving only and shall not export to MID's system; a Smart Contactor may be used to disconnect the ESS on voltage/frequency abnormality
ic.storage_specific_notes: Storage must be non-exporting (backup or peak shaving only) per MID Solar Electric Service Guide, Solar PV With Optional Energy Storage Systems, June 1 2019 (read from MID's azurewebsites dev mirror - re-verify against the current mid.org version). The guide shows five approved DG-with-battery interconnection configurations (Drawings PV-012.0 to PV-016.0). Since storage cannot export, a grid-charged battery earns no export credit; charging source is not otherwise restricted in the text read. Battery retrofit: the NEM 1.0 to NEM 2.0 trigger stated by MID is adding or rearranging panels that raise output by more than 10%; whether adding only a battery forces a NEM 1.0 customer onto NEM 2.0 is Unclear (not addressed on the pages read). ic.rule_summary: Irrigation district (publicly owned) outside CPUC jurisdiction. Retail net metering (Schedules RNT residential and NNT non-residential) is closed to new accounts (Secondary: closed at the start of 2015). New solar customers move to a Self-Generation rate schedule (DG domestic, CG commercial, FG farm, IG small industrial, HG large industrial, BG bulk industrial, MG municipal, SG) with Customer, Demand and TOU Energy charges. Netting is within each on-peak and off-peak period over the month; any monthly excess is credited at TID's Short Run Marginal Cost (published daily). No aggregation. System size not limited to load under the self-generation schedules, but TID reserves the right to require an interconnection study or limit size. Interconnection: Application for Interconnection, wiring diagram, inverter/panel spec sheets and CSI calculator report; TID field inspection before metering; TID Solar Installation Guidelines (2025) govern construction (one dedicated PV breaker per MSP, 120% bus rule, no line-side taps on residential). Adding generation to an existing solar service requires a new single-line diagram for approval.

No participation cap on Net Billing. Interconnection agreement for Net Billing covers renewable facilities of 1 MW or less. Applications only via PowerClerk (since 2024-01-01). Solar billing accounts set up after 2021-01-01 take NEM 2.0 (Developmental Schedule D-NEM): wholesale-based export credit - an hourly TOU 'ACC' (Annual Cash Compensation) rate paid for all energy sent back to the grid from a solar PV system each bill cycle. The ACC export rate is defined as paid for energy sent back to the grid 'from a solar photovoltaic system', which implies grid-charged battery exports are not the credited quantity, but no explicit grid-charging or metering rule was found - Unclear. ic.rule_summary: City-owned utility outside CPUC jurisdiction. Interconnection under RPU Electric Rule 22 'Distributed Generation Facilities Interconnection' (eff. 2022-05-10), a Rule 21-style process with Initial and Supplemental Review, non-export designation and certification/testing provisions. Export regime: Schedule SELF-GEN (eff. 2022-11-01; Board Res. 2022-1, Council Res. 23852) for renewable facilities up to 5,000 kW: all imports billed at the otherwise-applicable tariff (residential single-family assigned D-TOU); each kWh supplied to the grid is credited at the Avoided Cost of Energy (ACOE) - CAISO day-ahead LMP at the Vista take-out point plus capacity, ancillary, transmission, GHG, RPS and loss components, 3-year historical average, reset each July 1 - applied by TOU period; credits roll forward and any balance is PAID at termination of service. Sizing: up to 150% of annual consumption (more with proof of added load); maximum export to RPU's system 1,000 kW. Program cap 64 MW including existing Schedule NEM customers. Customers on an existing NEM agreement are not affected.

ic.rule_summary: EMC (NCUC-filed rate schedules, Docket EC-82 Sub 25; not subject to the Duke NMB/RSC order). Residential Net Metering Rider NM-R (eff. 4/1/2024): customer-side Renewable Generation (PV, fuel cell, micro-turbine, biomass, small wind; QF-eligible), customer must own the property; Option A (retail-rate kWh credit per billing month with $2.70/kW nameplate standby charge) CLOSED 4/1/2024; Option B (open since 7/1/2018): no standby charge, kWh delivered to the co-op credited at Rate Schedule AC avoided cost (two-channel billing, net monthly credit carried to next bill); switch options at most once a year on 60 days notice; customer keeps RECs; $100,000 homeowner liability insurance. Avoided cost (Schedule AC, eff. 2/1/2026) 5.058 c/kWh solar / 5.038 c/kWh non-solar, recalculated at least annually. Non-residential net metering is a pilot (NRNM). Small Generation Interconnection Standard (25 kW residential / 150 kW non-residential, single-phase): IEEE 1547 + UL 1741, lockable visible 'Generator Disconnect Switch', circuit saturation screens (30/60/100 kW per circuit by voltage), impact screens within 30 days, agreement within 10 days; application fee $250 residential / $500 non-residential (website; the 2019 standard PDF still says $100/$250). SGPPS 'sell all' rider to 20 kW residential / 100 kW non-residential.
ic.nem_cap_res_kw: Lesser of estimated max annual demand or 10 kW (Options A/B); Option B up to 25 kW after 10/1/2020
ic.nem_cap_nonres_kw: Individual basis above 100 kW (SGPPS); NRNM pilot limits not read
ic.export_credit_value: 5.058 c/kWh solar / 5.038 c/kWh non-solar avoided cost (Schedule AC eff. 2/1/2026), Option B; legacy Option A = retail energy charge
ic.ic_application_fee: $250 residential / $500 non-residential (non-refundable)
ic.ic_study_trigger_kw: 25 (residential; 150 kW non-residential) - above Small Generation Standard scope
ic.external_disconnect: Required - lockable visible-break 'Generator Disconnect Switch' near point of interconnection, accessible to co-op
ic.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - NM-R and the Small Generation Standard are silent on storage and on charging source
ic.standby_charge: Option A only: $2.70/kW nameplate per month (closed 4/1/2024); none for Option B
ic.storage_specific_notes: No storage provisions in NM-R, Schedule AC or the 2019 Interconnection Standard. Battery retrofit: Standard 4.10 prohibits changes to Generator output capacity or protection system without a new Application and new acceptance - so adding a battery that changes output capacity requires re-application; whether a legacy Option A (retail-credit) customer can keep Option A after re-applying, when Option A is closed to new service, is not stated (Unclear). Option B already credits exports at avoided cost, so little legacy value is at stake there.

ic.rule_summary: Distribution co-op (not PSC rate-regulated). Larger accounts may self-consume with no value for surplus.
ic.ic_application_fee: $150 + $50 per inspection

ic.rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 tiers (T1 <=10 kW, T2 <=100 kW, T3 <=2 MW AC; AC = DC x 0.85). Adds a sizing screen not in the rule: system must be estimated to produce <115% of annual kWh consumption; NEM systems >=50 kW must interconnect three-phase wye. Tier 2 fee $400, Tier 3 fee $1,000; Tier 2 insurance $1M. FPL requires a lockable visible-break manual disconnect for Tier 2 and Tier 3 (waived for inverter-based Tier 1 per rule).
ic.ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $400; Tier 3 $1,000 (plus study charge if required)
ic.external_disconnect: Required for Tier 2 and Tier 3 (adjacent to meter, lockable); waived Tier 1
ic.non_export_option: Yes for stand-alone batteries: grid-charged storage without renewables submits a Small Generator Interconnection Application; if non-exporting and no utility equipment needed, no interconnection agreement is required
ic.storage_specific_notes: FPL battery policy: battery paired with NEM renewable system is for customer use only and may NOT export to the grid (so battery energy never earns NEM credit); UL 1741 certification required, non-UL batteries must be DC-coupled behind a UL 1741 device; meter placard 'Battery storage utilized in this facility'. Tier 3 batteries reviewed in fast-track study. Stand-alone storage is not 'renewable' under 25-6.065(2)(d) and its output is not net metered. Adding a battery to an existing NEM system: no loss of NEM status stated (FL has no legacy/successor split); interconnection agreement sec. 7 requires a new application/agreement 30 days ahead only if gross power rating increases -- whether an AC-coupled battery counts as a rating increase is Unclear. Policy stated as subject to change.

Insurance T1 recommended $100k (not required), T2 $1M, T3 $2M. Tier 2/3 require externally accessible lockable manual AC load-break disconnect (not a breaker) near meter. Service-drop screen: PV rating <=90% of transformer/service rating or customer pays upgrade. Tier 1 PTO usually within 10 business days of completion.
ic.ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $240; Tier 3 $750
ic.external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 and Tier 3 (visible-break, lockable, labeled Generator Disconnect Switch); not required Tier 1
ic.storage_specific_notes: DEF net-metering tier pages and application do not address batteries (unlike FPL, no published battery-export prohibition found). Whether battery export earns NEM credit, whether grid charging is permitted on a NEM account, and whether adding a battery to an existing NEM system requires a new application: all Unclear from DEF published material. No legacy/successor NEM split in FL, so no grandfathering to lose. DEF runs EnergyWise Home Battery Control DR (see programs).

ic.rule_summary: Follows FPSC Rule 25-6.065 via Rate Schedule NM-1 and Standard Interconnection Agreements (Tier 1 <=10 kW, Tier 2 >10-100 kW, Tier 3 >100 kW-2 MW AC; GPR = DC x 0.85; GPR <=90% of service rating). Utility-set fees: Tier 2 $250 one-time (no charge for any Tier 2 study); Tier 3 $500 + study deposit $3,000 (actual cost, capped $3,000). Insurance T2 $1M, T3 $2M (self-insurance by approval). Visible load-break lockable manual disconnect adjacent to meter required T2/T3. Agreement executed within 30 days (90 if Tier 3 study); PTO notice within 10 business days. Agreements still cite IEEE 1547-2003/UL 1741-2005.
ic.ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $250; Tier 3 $500 + study up to $3,000 (deposit $3,000)
ic.ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier 3; Tier 2 study at no charge if needed)
ic.external_disconnect: Required Tier 2 and Tier 3 (visible load-break, lockable, exterior adjacent to meter)
ic.storage_specific_notes: Agreements define RGS as renewable generation only; batteries not addressed in NM-1 agreements read. TECO Steps to Connect page reportedly states batteries are interconnected but not net metered (search-snippet only; page could not be loaded, redirect loop) -- implies battery discharge does not earn NEM credit: Unverified. Adding a battery: agreement sec. 7 requires a new application 30 days ahead only for a change in GPR; whether a battery changes GPR is Unclear. No legacy NEM tier to lose in FL.

ic.rule_summary: Municipal; exempt from FPSC Rule 25-6.065 (s. 366.91(6) F.S. requires own program). JEA Distributed Generation Policy eff. 2018-04-01 replaced net metering: monthly netting but exported kWh credited at JEA fuel rate (~3c/kWh at launch) instead of retail; credits accrue through calendar year and remaining balance paid at year end per policy. Systems passing final inspection by 2018-03-31 grandfathered under retired Net Metering Policy (Tiers 1-3, full retail) for 20 years; 10 MW aggregate cap applied to legacy Tier 1-3 net metering. Interconnection via PowerClerk; JEA DER Technical Interconnection & Interoperability Requirements (2025).
ic.nem_aggregate_cap: 10 MW aggregate for legacy Tier 1-3 net metering (closed 2018)
ic.export_credit_value: Exports credited at JEA fuel charge rate (post-2018-04-01 systems); legacy NM systems full retail through 20-yr grandfather
ic.external_disconnect: Required (utility disconnect); separate battery load disconnect if permanently mounted battery(ies) (per JEA DER requirements, search snippet)
ic.storage_specific_notes: Adding a battery to a legacy (pre-4/1/2018) net-metered system: JEA pages state (per search snippet) that a grandfathered NM customer who takes JEA Battery Incentive loses grandfathering and moves to the Distributed Generation (fuel-rate) program -- the retrofit trigger is taking the incentive; whether a self-funded battery retrofit also forfeits grandfathering is Unclear. JEA itself framed batteries as a way to self-consume rather than export at fuel rate (2018 rebate up to $4,000, first 50). jea.com blocks automated fetch (CAPTCHA) so policy text not read directly.

ic.rule_summary: Municipal; own TruNet Solar net metering program (s. 366.91(6) F.S.). Tiers by AC gross power rating mirror FPSC tiers: Tier 1 0-10 kW no fee; Tier 2 >10-100 kW $340; Tier 3 >100 kW-2 MW $1,300. Systems connected/approved by 2025-06-30 grandfathered at full retail through 2045-06-30. Systems interconnected after 2025-06-30: full retail during grace period through 2026-10-31, then Community Solar Energy rate through 2030-06-30, then Retail Levelized Fuel rate. From 2026-11-01 exports credited within the same billing period (no kWh rollover); leftover $ credit carries forward on account. Annual true-up done Dec 2025 plus a final true-up Fall 2026. Sizing: capacity should not exceed home energy needs. MID-TRANSITION: successor rates take effect Nov 2026.
ic.export_credit_value: Legacy (<=2025-06-30): full retail ~10.7c/kWh residential through 2045; new: full retail to 2026-10-31, then Community Solar Energy rate (~4.6c/kWh per program chunk, Secondary) to 2030-06-30, then Retail Levelized Fuel rate
ic.ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $340; Tier 3 $1,300
ic.storage_specific_notes: Battery retrofit on legacy system: taking OUC Battery Storage Rebate requires forfeiting TruNet Full Retail Rate (10.7c/kWh) on all exports -- i.e., a rebated battery retrofit loses grandfathering. An add-on PV array does NOT affect grandfathered status (OUC FAQ); whether a self-funded (non-rebate) battery retrofit affects grandfathering is not stated: Unclear. Applications may be solar or solar+battery. Grid-charging rules not published.

ic.rule_summary: Municipal (City of Lakeland); own Net Metering Service schedule Sheets 8.4-8.6 (eff. 2023-10-01). PV only (static inverters). Tiers: T1 <=10 kW, T2 <=100 kW (residential), T3 <=2 MW (commercial). Sizing: PV may not exceed 100% of annual consumption; >90% of transformer/service capacity at customer expense. Exports metered on separate register and credited at full retail; kWh credits carry forward on a moving 12-month window and expire unpaid at end of window (no annual cash-out); on termination accumulated credit paid at full retail. No aggregate cap currently (utility may limit). 12-month minimum term; city may terminate on 30 days notice. Insurance T2 up to $1M, T3 up to $2M, T1 recommended. Manual lockable visible load-break disconnect required all tiers. Standards cite IEEE 1547-2003/UL 1741 (2005). MANDATORY RATE: residential solar customers must take Rate RSD (Residential Service Demand): $14.45/mo + $6.69/kW billing demand less Value of Solar Credit $0.92/kW + 2.674c/kWh energy (eff. 2025-10-01); legacy pre-2016 RS solar customers moved to RSD from 2026-01-01.
ic.nem_aggregate_cap: None currently (utility reserves right to limit)
ic.export_credit_value: Full retail kWh credit (separate register); moving 12-month carryforward; unused credits forfeited (no cash-out) except full-retail payout on termination
ic.ic_application_fee: Not stated; Interconnection Study Charge possible for Tier 2/3
ic.external_disconnect: Required all tiers (manual, lockable, visible load-break)
ic.standby_charge: Residential solar customers mandatorily billed on demand rate RSD ($6.69/kW billing demand, $0.92/kW Value of Solar Credit); standby service not permitted on RSD
ic.standby_threshold_kw: 0 (all residential PV)
ic.storage_specific_notes: Net Metering schedule applies to PV arrays only; storage not addressed in tariff sheets read (program chunk cites an "Agreement for Parallel Connection of PV and/or ESS" -- not read). Mandatory demand rate (RSD) makes battery peak-shaving valuable for residential PV customers. Customer must notify city of any change to PV system; effect of adding a battery on net metering status: Unclear. Grid charging / battery export credit: Unclear.

ic.rule_summary: Municipal (City of Gainesville d/b/a GRU); own Agreement for Interconnection and Parallel Operation of Distributed Generation Resources (s. 366.91(6) F.S.), not FPSC 25-6.065. Tiers sized in kW DC (not AC): T1 <=10 kW DC, T2 >10-100 kW DC ($400 fee), T3 >100 kW-2 MW DC ($1,000 fee). NEM ENDED for new systems: GRU Authority resolution 2024-04-17 -- excess kWh now credited at GRU's current fuel adjustment rate (not retail); monthly credit rolls to next bill; annual calendar-year true-up converted to cash at GRU avoided cost price (GRU may change without notice). Existing (pre-change) solar customers reported unaffected (Secondary). Pre-application Letter of Intent / circuit capacity check required (approval valid 1 yr); GRU enforces circuit hosting limits. Technical review ~4-5 weeks. Lockable visible load-break 'Auxiliary Generation Disconnect' within 10 ft and on same wall as meter required. Telemetry at owner cost >=250 kW DC. Customer keeps RECs. Insurance: web page says T1 $100k, T2 $1M, T3 $2M; 2022 agreement text says T1 $100k, T2 $300k, T3 $1M (current 04/08/2024 agreement is image-only, not read).
ic.export_credit_value: GRU fuel adjustment rate (~3.5c/kWh at April 2024 adoption, varies monthly); year-end balance cashed out at GRU avoided cost
ic.ic_application_fee: Tier 1 $0; Tier 2 $400; Tier 3 $1,000 (non-refundable) + system impact study at customer cost if needed; $100 missed meter-set fee
ic.ic_study_trigger_kw: Utility discretion (study if initial feasibility evaluation inconclusive; circuit capacity pre-check for all sizes)
ic.external_disconnect: Required all tiers (manual, lockable, visible load-break, within 10 ft of meter, labeled 'Auxiliary Generation Disconnect')
ic.storage_specific_notes: Agreement defines DGR as a renewable generation system; NEM web page and agreement do not mention batteries at all -- export credit for battery discharge, grid charging, and storage sizing all Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing system: agreement sec. 10.3 requires prompt notice of any modification changing configuration/rating/operation and GRU may audit before reconnection; sec. 9.1.5 lets GRU disconnect for unapproved modifications. Whether a battery retrofit moves a pre-April-2024 retail-NEM customer onto the fuel-rate credit is not stated: Unclear. With exports at ~fuel rate, storage self-consumption is the main value lever.
