ic.rule_summary: Municipal; own Solar Net Metering Agreement (Rev 5, 08/02/2019) under s. 366.91(6) F.S., not FPSC 25-6.065 tiers. PV systems up to 100 kWac only (single agreement, no tiers); single-phase allowed up to 15 kWac, three-phase balanced above. No fee for application or net meter. Excess kWh credited at applicable retail tariff (city says full retail value incl. taxes) and carried forward on a rolling 12-month window; unused credits forfeited to the City at end of window, never paid. City retains RECs. Insurance: general liability >= $100,000 (homeowner policy may satisfy) for all sizes. Physical isolation: either a manual lockable load-break disconnect adjacent to meter, OR elect meter removal as the isolation means (no switch). City may terminate agreement on 30 days notice for any reason. Standards cited are dated (UL 1741, IEEE 929-2000, IEEE 1262-1995).
ic.export_credit_value: Full retail kWh credit (rolling 12-month carryforward; unused credits forfeited, no cash-out)
ic.ic_application_fee: $0 (no application or net meter charge)
ic.external_disconnect: Owner's choice: manual lockable load-break disconnect adjacent to meter, OR allow City to pull the net meter as isolation (no switch needed)
ic.storage_specific_notes: Agreement and application define the system as PV only (static inverter), but the application form has a 'Batteries (if applicable)' field, so PV+battery is interconnected under the same agreement. No rule on battery export credit or grid charging: Unclear. Adding a battery to an existing net-metered system: agreement sec. 3.D says the agreement TERMINATES upon any modification or alteration of the PV system and a new Solar Net Metering Agreement is required (sec. 4.A notice). Because terms are unchanged for new agreements (no legacy/successor split), re-signing should not lose export value, but whether a battery counts as a 'modification' is not stated -- treat as requiring a new agreement.

ic.rule_summary: Co-op; own Net Metering Rider and single-form "Interconnection and Parallel Operation of Renewable Distribution Generation" agreement (rev. 10/22/19) instead of FPSC 25-6.065 tiered agreements. Net meter measures delivered and received kWh; excess over the year purchased at year end at the avoided cost of wholesale supplier Seminole Electric Cooperative. Agreement: 1-yr auto-renewing term; co-op may terminate service at its sole discretion or disconnect without notice for safety; access required for WREC and Seminole; no intentional islanding (IEEE 1547). Tier sizes, fees and insurance not stated in agreement; Net Metering Rider text not read.

ic.rule_summary: Co-op (Sumter Electric Cooperative d/b/a SECO Energy); own Net Metering tariff Sheet 16.4 + Interconnection Agreement Sheets 17.0-17.5 (eff. 2022-04-01) under Seminole Electric wholesale contract. Tiers per 25-6.065 but capped at 1,000 kW AC (not 2 MW); GPR (DC x 0.85) <=90% of service rating. Net billing, not retail NEM: all kWh taken from grid billed at otherwise applicable rate; excess kWh delivered to grid in each billing cycle credited at base cost of power (Schedule PCA) + monthly WPCA factor (wholesale/avoided cost). Credits only to the service behind which system sits. Insurance: none <=10 kW, $1M >10 kW (co-op as additional insured). Lockable manual disconnect separate from meter socket required for all sizes. IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 latest version. AMI bi-directional meter required. PTO within 10 business days.
ic.export_credit_value: Excess kWh each billing cycle credited at Schedule PCA base cost of power + WPCA factor (wholesale power cost), not retail
ic.external_disconnect: Required all tiers (lockable manual disconnect, separate from meter socket, readily accessible)
ic.storage_specific_notes: SECO interconnection agreement explicitly lists "battery storage" among RGS energy sources (rare in FL) -- battery may interconnect under the standard agreement. Because exports are credited at wholesale cost of power in the same billing cycle (net billing), battery self-consumption shifting has value; whether grid-charged battery exports are credited is not addressed: Unclear. MLGW-specific deviations: three interconnection options, all dual-metered with a separate generation meter: (A) Self-Generation -- excess flows to grid WITHOUT compensation; (B) DPP sell-all to TVA; (C) Self-Generation + DPP sell-excess. Options A and C carry a monthly Electric Service Availability charge (residential $14.40/mo; non-residential varies by rate, from $32.00/mo for GSA part 1; subject to change). Application fee: residential $250 + $5/kW, non-residential $500 + $5/kW (check only). Customer pays construction quote (generation meter + socket, meter labor, any upgrades, one System Acceptance Test); $200 per re-test ($200 initial test waived for TVA Green Connect QCN projects). Technical review ~4-5 weeks; interconnection study at MLGW discretion by size/location. Interconnection and Parallel Operation Agreement + liability insurance documentation required (amount not read).

market.struct: $/MWh payment for reserve capacity deliverable within 30 minutes
market.val: Not independently confirmed for 2026; published via PJM Data Miner 2 Day-Ahead Ancillary Service LMPs feed
market.limits: 30-minute response requirement
market.tariff: OATT Schedule 1
market.stack: Synchronized Reserve;Non-Synchronized Reserve

market.n: Synchronized Reserve Market (Tier 1 and Tier 2)
market.struct: $/MWh capacity payment cleared in the 10-minute co-optimized reserve market; Tier 1 is spare energy from online resources deliverable within 10 minutes while Tier 2 is called only when Tier 1 is insufficient
market.val: Clearing prices vary by hour and reserve zone and were not independently confirmed for 2026; PJM added a 30% adder to the Synchronized Reserve requirement in May 2023 after under-performance during reserve events
market.limits: Must respond within 10 minutes and sustain for the event duration; deployed via a PJM-declared Synchronized Reserve Event
market.tariff: OATT Schedule 1; Manual 11 Section 8
market.stack: Regulation;Capacity Performance;Energy Arbitrage

market.n: DER and Aggregation Participation Model - Energy (LBMP)
market.struct: $/MWh Day-Ahead and Real-Time LBMP settled at the Aggregation's Transmission Node; dispatch-only (no start-up/commitment parameters)
market.limits: Min 10 kW per individual DER asset (Services Tariff 4.1.10.1); max Injection Limit 20 MW per facility; six-second real-time telemetry required for each Aggregation plus hourly revenue-quality meter data by noon next business day; Aggregator must be reachable 24x7 for verbal real-time operations; Demand Reductions below the Monthly Net Benefit Threshold are not eligible for energy payments unless dispatched for reliability
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10, 4.5.2, 4.5.7, 17; Aggregation Manual Sections 2.2.1, 6.1.10, 6.2
market.export: Settled at Transmission Node LBMP; withdrawals by Withdrawal-Eligible Generators treated as negative generation
market.stack: ICAP market participation (required to also be in Energy market); NOT stackable with SCR or EDRP - a Resource may not simultaneously be a DER in an Aggregation and an SCR/EDRP Resource (Aggregation Manual 4.3.2); dual participation with utility CSRP/DLRP/DLM permitted with notice

market.n: DER and Aggregation Participation Model - Installed Capacity (ICAP) Supplier
market.struct: $/kW-month UCAP sold into Strip, Monthly and ICAP Spot Market auctions; UCAP = Aggregation ICAP x Capacity Accreditation Factor x derating factor
market.limits: Aggregation must submit DMNC test data per season; at least one DER in the Aggregation must be participating in the capacity market; ICAP participation requires simultaneous Energy market participation; new ICAP suppliers must run one month in the Energy market first; ICAP Suppliers must bid the ICAP-equivalent of UCAP sold into the Day-Ahead Market every hour (or schedule a bilateral, or notify NYISO of an outage); two-year outage schedule required at enrollment
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 5.12.1.3, 5.12.3, 5.12.7, 5.12.13.1; ICAP Manual Sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.8; ICAP Manual Attachment J Sections 3.0 and 6.9; Aggregation Manual Section 2.2.5
market.stack: ICAP + Energy + Ancillary Services simultaneously; NOT stackable with SCR (an SCR must separate in DRIS before transitioning; a DER that exits must give notice by Aug 1 and can only rejoin SCR the following May 1)

market.n: DER and Aggregation Participation Model - Ancillary Services (Regulation and Operating Reserves)
market.struct: $/MWh market clearing price for Regulation Capacity/Movement and for 10-Minute Spinning, 10-Minute Non-Synchronized, 30-Minute Synchronized and 30-Minute Non-Synchronized Reserves
market.limits: Under current (pre-Order-2222) rules every individual DER in the Aggregation must itself be capable of the service offered - the Aggregation can only offer the lowest-quality product common to all its members (Aggregation Manual 2.2.4); Aggregations providing reserves or regulation must bid self-committed flexible; self-committed fixed and ISO-committed fixed bid modes are ineligible for Operating Reserves; new reserve Aggregations verify performance during the first two weeks of the first active month rather than prequalifying
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 15.4.1.2.4 and Rate Schedule 4; Aggregation Manual Section 2.2.4; Ancillary Services Manual Section 6.12.2
market.stack: Energy + ICAP + Ancillary Services can be provided by the same Aggregation; the all-members-capable restriction is scheduled to change with NYISO's Order 2222 implementation

market.n: Dual Participation - NYISO Aggregation plus utility DR program (CSRP / DLRP / DLM)
market.struct: No separate payment - this is the rule permitting a DER to earn both NYISO market revenue and utility DR program revenue
market.limits: PERMITTED. An Aggregation containing DER that also participate in programs meeting distribution-system needs in the NYCA must notify NYISO of dual participation at enrollment (Market Participant User's Guide Section 1.2); the Aggregation's NYISO offers must be constructed so the Aggregation is scheduled by NYISO whenever it operates to meet the non-wholesale commitment (Services Tariff 4.1.11). NYISO confirms CSRP, DLRP and DLM are covered by this categorization. Dual-participation requirements are scheduled to change when NYISO implements its Order 2222-compliant tariff (targeted end of 2026)
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 4.1.11; Market Participant User's Guide Section 1.2
market.stack: Con Edison CSRP; Con Edison DLRP; Joint Utilities Dynamic Load Management (DLM); NOT stackable with NYISO SCR or EDRP

market.n: DER Aggregation - Telemetry and Metering Requirements
market.struct: Cost gate, not a revenue stream
market.limits: Six-second real-time telemetry (a meter read every six seconds) required for each Aggregation, plus hourly revenue-quality meter data. Four telemetry channels required regardless of composition: Energy injections, Energy withdrawals, Demand Reductions, and total response MW (zeros for non-applicable channels), plus a point for actual Aggregation load. NYISO sends Base Point Signals to the Aggregation, not to individual DER. End-to-End Communication Testing among Aggregator control center, Member System (TO) and NYISO required for every new Aggregation enrollment; adding a DER to an existing Aggregation does not require re-testing. Meter Authority must be an authorized Meter Services Entity, the municipal utility, or the Member System
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10.4, 13, 13.3.2, 13.3.2.1; Aggregation Manual Section 7.3; Revenue Metering Requirements Manual; Accounting and Billing Manual Section 3.2.1
market.stack: Applies to all Aggregation market participation (Energy, AS, ICAP)

market.n: Energy Storage Resource (ESR) in an Aggregation - retail-rate charging (Order 841)
market.struct: Charging energy purchased at the applicable retail rate rather than wholesale LBMP
market.limits: Aggregations containing withdrawal-capable DER (Energy Storage Resources) may withdraw energy at retail rates per FERC Order No. 841; the Aggregation must supply the LSE PTID of the relevant retail authority for settlement. An Aggregation may be a Single Resource Type Aggregation of only ESRs, or a heterogeneous DER Aggregation mixing ESR, Intermittent Power Resources and Demand Side Resources
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 7.2.8
market.stack: Energy arbitrage + ICAP + Ancillary Services from the same ESR Aggregation

market.n: Behind-the-Meter Net Generation (BTM:NG) Resource - exclusion from DER model
market.struct: Participates as a BTM:NG Resource rather than as a DER; not eligible for the Aggregation model
market.limits: A BTM:NG Resource routinely serves its host load from an on-site generation source, which precludes it from the DER participation model. A BTM:NG Resource that converts to a DER must thereafter routinely serve its host load by withdrawing from the grid rather than from on-site generation
market.tariff: Aggregation Manual Section 4.3.3
market.stack: Not stackable with the DER Aggregation model

market.n: Installed Capacity - Special Case Resources (ICAP-SCR)
market.struct: Monthly $/kW-month UCAP capacity payment from ICAP auctions plus per-event energy payment at LBMP with a daily Minimum Payment Nomination (strike price) guarantee
market.val: Capacity: monthly UCAP price from the ICAP Spot Market Auction for the resource's Load Zone (see per-zone price rows). Energy: real-time zonal LBMP with a daily guarantee of Minimum Payment Nomination recovery and a guaranteed four-hour minimum payment period
market.limits: Minimum 100 kW load reduction in aggregate by Load Zone; mandatory performance for a minimum of four hours when NYISO calls a reliability event; day-ahead advisory plus 2-hour in-day notice; SCRs activated before EDRP resources; must demonstrate maximum capacity obligation in each Capability Period (test or event at least once every six months); all SCRs carry a 4-hour duration requirement and are accredited commensurate with other four-hour resources; event/test meter data due within 75 days; failure to respond derates the resource and reduces future UCAP payments
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 5.12.11, 5.12.13.1; ICAP Manual Section 4.12; Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7)
market.stack: May enroll simultaneously in ONE reliability-based program (SCR or EDRP) and ONE economic-based program (DADRP or DSASP); SCR energy payments are netted against any concurrent DADRP/DSASP payments and only reduction above the DADRP/DSASP schedule earns SCR energy payment (EDRP Manual 5.4.2). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model - a Resource cannot be both an SCR and a DER at the same time

market.n: Emergency Demand Response Program (EDRP)
market.struct: $/MWh energy-only payment for verified load reduction during a NYISO-called reliability event; no capacity payment
market.val: Greater of the real-time zonal LBMP or $500/MWh, with a guaranteed four-hour minimum payment period
market.limits: Minimum 100 kW load reduction; participation in any event is VOLUNTARY and there are no non-performance penalties; 2-hour in-day event notice; EDRP resources are activated after SCR resources; hourly interval metering required; event meter data due within 75 days; no capacity payment
market.tariff: Services Tariff Attachment G Section 22.10; Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7) Sections 2.2, 4.3, 5.4.2
market.stack: One reliability program (EDRP or SCR) may be combined with one economic program (DADRP or DSASP); EDRP energy payment is reduced by any concurrent DADRP/DSASP payment (EDRP Manual 5.4.2). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model

market.n: Day-Ahead Demand Response Program (DADRP)
market.struct: $/MWh Day-Ahead LBMP for scheduled load reduction plus a daily Curtailment Initiation Cost guarantee
market.val: Day-Ahead LBMP times the lesser of actual or Day-Ahead scheduled load reduction; plus Curtailment Initiation Cost paid on a daily basis where applicable
market.limits: Minimum 1 MW reduction in aggregate by Load Zone and LSE; offers must be at or above the Monthly Net Benefit Offer Floor (MNBT); accepted offers notified by 11:00 a.m. for the next day midnight-to-midnight; response is MANDATORY when scheduled and penalties may apply if scheduled curtailment does not physically occur; hourly interval metering; CBL baseline (highest five of last ten like days); economic schedule meter data due within 55 days; no capacity payment; no real-time schedule
market.tariff: Day-Ahead Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 5); Technical Bulletin 245 (MNBT)
market.stack: One economic program (DADRP or DSASP) may be combined with one reliability program (SCR or EDRP). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model

market.n: Demand Side Ancillary Services Program (DSASP)
market.struct: $/MWh marginal clearing price for the Operating Reserve or Regulation product scheduled; no energy payment for the underlying reduction
market.val: Reserve or Regulation market clearing price by location and product
market.limits: Minimum 1 MW reduction in aggregate by Load Zone; minimum energy offer at the Monthly Net Benefit Offer Floor; mandatory performance when scheduled and penalties may apply; requires 6-second two-way telemetry plus a revenue-grade interval billing meter and an instantaneous total load meter; must respond to 5-minute RTD base points for Reserves and 6-second AGC base points for Regulation; only interruptible load may supply Spinning Reserve or Regulation - loads backed by a qualified Local Generator may only supply Non-Synchronized Reserves; real-time baseline (actual load just prior to the real-time schedule); no capacity payment
market.tariff: Ancillary Services Manual; Services Tariff Rate Schedules 3 and 4
market.stack: One economic program (DSASP or DADRP) may be combined with one reliability program (SCR or EDRP). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model

market.n: Targeted Demand Response Program (TDRP)
market.struct: Energy payment at the rate of whichever program (SCR or EDRP) the resource is enrolled in; no separate TDRP payment
market.limits: Effective July 1 2007. Con Edison may request NYISO to activate demand response for local reliability in specific sub-load pockets of Load Zone J (New York City). Only existing SCR and EDRP resources in those locations are eligible, and participation is VOLUNTARY for both. TDRP responses cannot set the real-time market price. CSPs with resources in sub-load pockets are notified through the standard EDRP advisory process
market.tariff: Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7) Section 6
market.stack: Layered on top of an existing SCR or EDRP enrollment; not a standalone enrollment

market.n: Small Customer Aggregation (SCR / EDRP)
market.struct: Same payment as the underlying SCR or EDRP enrollment; this is a measurement and verification accommodation, not a separate revenue stream
market.limits: Allows resources with an ACL below the DRIS minimum kW limit to be aggregated and to use alternative validation methods such as statistical sampling to claim performance on a portfolio basis, in lieu of individual interval meters. Available for EDRP and SCR resources only (not DADRP or DSASP). Program-level minimums still apply at the aggregation level
market.tariff: Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7) Section 2.7
market.stack: Underlying SCR or EDRP program rules apply

market.n: ICAP Spot Market Auction - New York City (Zone J / NYC Locality) UCAP price
market.struct: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction; the price an SCR or a DER Aggregation with CRIS in Zone J receives per kW of UCAP sold
market.val: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $32.59, Jun $32.53, Jul $12.41, Aug $12.35, Sep $12.39 per kW-month. Winter 2025-26: Nov 2025 $6.44, Dec 2025 $6.41, Jan 2026 $6.25, Feb 2026 $6.25, Mar 2026 $6.24, Apr 2026 $6.26 per kW-month. Summer 2025 for comparison: May $14.96, Jun $15.93, Jul $15.93, Aug $15.86, Oct $15.57 per kW-month
market.limits: Prices are monthly UCAP clearing prices. Summer Capability Period runs May through October; Winter Capability Period runs November through April. May and June 2026 were record NYC prices driven by a Locational Capacity Requirement increase and near-zero excess (0.06% and 0.09% above requirement). Selling capacity requires CRIS; a DER of 2 MW or less can obtain CRIS without a deliverability study
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
market.stack: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation; energy and ancillary services revenue on top of capacity

market.n: ICAP Spot Market Auction - Long Island (Zone K / LI Locality) UCAP price
market.struct: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction for the Long Island locality
market.val: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $11.11, Jun $11.70, Jul $10.46, Aug $10.13, Sep $10.13 per kW-month. Winter 2025-26: LI cleared at the NYCA price - Nov 2025 $1.80, Dec 2025 $3.65, Jan 2026 $3.73, Feb 2026 $3.74, Mar 2026 $2.64, Apr 2026 $1.82 per kW-month. Summer 2025: LI cleared at the NYCA price of $5.23-$6.04 per kW-month
market.limits: Long Island separates from the NYCA price only when the LI locality binds, which in the observed data happened in the Summer 2026 Capability Period but not in Winter 2025-26 or Summer 2025. Summer Capability Period runs May through October
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
market.stack: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation

market.n: ICAP Spot Market Auction - G-J Locality (Lower Hudson Valley + NYC) UCAP price
market.struct: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction for the G-J Locality (Zones G through J)
market.val: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $7.92, Jun $7.87, Jul $4.14, Aug $4.53, Sep $5.97 per kW-month. Winter 2025-26: Nov 2025 $1.80, Dec 2025 $3.65, Jan 2026 $3.73, Feb 2026 $3.74, Mar 2026 $2.64, Apr 2026 $1.82 per kW-month. Summer 2025: May $5.23, Jun $5.46, Jul $5.47, Aug $6.04, Oct $5.86 per kW-month
market.limits: In every month observed (Nov 2025 through Sep 2026) the G-J Locality cleared at the same price as NYCA/Rest of State, meaning the G-J constraint was not binding separately. Zone J prices are set separately and are much higher. Summer Capability Period runs May through October
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
market.stack: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation

market.n: ICAP Spot Market Auction - NYCA / Rest of State (upstate) UCAP price
market.struct: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction for the NYCA-wide (Rest of State) market
market.val: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $7.92, Jun $7.87, Jul $4.14, Aug $4.53, Sep $5.97 per kW-month (ROS price paid by LSEs, weighted average, equals the NYCA price in each of these months). Winter 2025-26: Nov 2025 $1.80, Dec 2025 $3.65, Jan 2026 $3.73, Feb 2026 $3.74, Mar 2026 $2.64, Apr 2026 $1.82 per kW-month. Summer 2025: May $5.23, Jun $5.46, Jul $5.47, Aug $6.04, Oct $5.86 per kW-month
market.limits: Upstate/Rest-of-State capacity is worth roughly one quarter to one fifth of New York City capacity in the Summer 2026 Capability Period. Summer Capability Period runs May through October; Winter runs November through April. Monthly auction; UCAP not ICAP
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
market.stack: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation

market.n: ICAP market - Strip and Monthly (Capability Period) Auctions
market.struct: $/kW-month UCAP price from the Capability Period Auction (strip) or the Monthly Auction, as an alternative or supplement to the Spot Market Auction
market.limits: Aggregations and SCRs may offer into the Strip (Capability Period) Auction, the Monthly Auction, and the ICAP Spot Market Auction, or sell capacity bilaterally. Unsold UCAP is automatically offered into the Spot Market Auction
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 5.14; ICAP Manual Section 4; Aggregation Manual Section 2.2.5
market.stack: SCR program; DER Aggregation ICAP participation; bilateral capacity contracts

market.n: FERC Order 2222 implementation status - DER Participation Model
market.struct: Rule / timeline row - no direct payment
market.limits: Timeline: NYISO filed its Aggregation participation model June 27 2019 (Docket ER19-2276); FERC accepted it January 23 2020 (170 FERC 61033). NYISO filed its Order 2222 compliance filing July 19 2021; FERC accepted it June 17 2022 while directing 30+ further tariff modifications. FERC granted NYISO an extension to December 31 2026 to complete full Order 2222 compliance. NYISO filed further DER tariff revisions June 1 2023 (Docket ER23-2040); FERC accepted them April 15 2024 (187 FERC 61022) and expressly found the 10 kW minimum capability requirement just and reasonable and NOT a temporary measure, while directing an informational report which NYISO filed April 15 2026. The DER and Aggregation participation model is LIVE today under the interim (pre-Order-2222) rules; dual-participation, operating-reserve composition and other rules change when the Order 2222-compliant tariff takes effect
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 through 4.1.10.7.3; FERC Docket Nos. ER19-2276, ER21-2460, ER23-2040
market.stack: Interim rules apply until the Order 2222-compliant tariff is implemented (targeted end of 2026)

market.n: Small Utility opt-in gate for DER Aggregation participation
market.struct: Eligibility gate - no payment
market.limits: New York has NO statewide opt-out of third-party aggregation of retail customers. The only gate is the Order 2222 small-utility provision: a Resource that is a customer of a Small Utility may not be enrolled in an Aggregation unless the Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authority affirmatively authorizes (opts in to) such participation. NYISO defines Small Utility as a Distribution Utility that distributed four million MWh or less in NYISO's immediately prior completed fiscal year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). The determination applies for the forthcoming Capability Year. If a RERRA later withdraws authorization and the Aggregator notifies NYISO before April 1, the DER is ineligible from the first day of the following Capability Year; if notice comes on or after April 1 but before May 1, the DER is ineligible as of June 1
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 4.1.10 (definitions of Distribution Utility and Small Utility)
market.stack: Customers of New York's large investor-owned distribution utilities (over 4 million MWh/yr) face no opt-in gate and may join an Aggregation directly

market.n: Prohibition on duplicative compensation - same service in wholesale and retail
market.struct: Stacking gate - no payment
market.limits: A DER may not provide the SAME service in the NYISO-administered markets that it already provides in a retail service or program. FERC struck NYISO's originally proposed broader phrase or substantially similar as an improperly broad restriction, so the bar is same service only. The Aggregator must attest at enrollment that DER enrolled in its Aggregation are not providing the same service in a retail service or program, and must attest to compliance with the Distribution Utilities' tariffs and the RERRA's rules
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10.5 and 4.1.10.6
market.stack: Different services (e.g. NYISO energy plus a retail locational or environmental credit) may be stacked; identical services may not

market.n: Stacking NYISO DER Aggregation with NY retail VDER Value Stack
market.struct: Retail VDER credits stacked on top of NYISO wholesale revenue
market.limits: Per the NY Joint Utilities DERA Duplicative Compensation Matrix (June 30 2025): VDER Energy and Capacity components are Utility Only and CANNOT be stacked with NYISO DERA. VDER Environmental Value (REC), Demand Reduction Value (DRV), Locational System Relief Value (LSRV), Market Transition Credit, Community Credit and Non-Mass Market Community Credit ARE stackable with a NYISO DER Aggregation. For storage, DRV, LSRV, MTC and Non-Mass Market Community Credit are stackable. Net Energy Metering is Utility Only and NOT stackable. Customers taking service under a utility Buyback Tariff are not eligible to participate in the NYISO DER aggregation model per tariff. Applicable retail tariffs are WVS and WDS (import and export) for storage; WDS tariffs are not yet approved or filed at FERC for all utilities
market.tariff: NY PSC VDER Value Stack; utility WVS and WDS tariffs; NYISO Services Tariff 4.1.10.6
market.export: VDER Value Stack energy and capacity components are forfeited if the DER sells energy or capacity into NYISO through an Aggregation
market.stack: VDER DRV; VDER LSRV; VDER Environmental Value/REC; VDER Market Transition Credit; VDER Community Credit; Non-Wires Alternative contracts

market.n: Stacking NYISO DER Aggregation with utility demand response programs (CSRP / DLRP / DLM)
market.struct: Utility DR capacity and energy payments stacked on top of NYISO wholesale revenue
market.limits: Per the NY Joint Utilities DERA Duplicative Compensation Matrix (June 30 2025): utility Demand Response Program CAPACITY payments are stackable with a NYISO DER Aggregation for Demand Reduction, Generator and Energy Storage resource types. Utility Demand Response Program ENERGY payments are stackable but the resource is ineligible for the utility performance payment in hours with overlapping NYISO energy payments. Non-Wires Alternative contracts are stackable for all resource types including Landfill Gas. Separately, NYISO's own DR programs (SCR and EDRP) are marked fully stackable with utility DR programs during NYISO's interim market
market.tariff: Services Tariff Section 4.1.11 (dual participation notice); NY Joint Utilities DERA Duplicative Compensation Matrix
market.stack: Con Edison CSRP; Con Edison DLRP; Joint Utilities Dynamic Load Management; utility Non-Wires Alternative contracts

market.n: DER Aggregation - eligibility sizing rules (10 kW DER / 100 kW Aggregation / 20 MW injection cap)
market.struct: Eligibility gate - no payment
market.limits: Minimum capability of each individual DER (including a Demand Side Resource) participating in an Aggregation is 10 kW; where a DER includes multiple assets of different technologies at the facility, EACH asset must independently meet 10 kW. Minimum size of a DER Aggregation is 100 kW; an Aggregation that offers a combination of Energy injections, Energy withdrawals and/or Demand Reduction must be able to offer at least 100 kW of each. Maximum Injection Limit for an injecting facility in an Aggregation is 20 MW; there is no size cap on Demand Reduction resources. All DER in an Aggregation must be on the SAME Transmission Node and therefore in the same NYISO Load Zone. A DER facility has a single point of interconnection and a single utility account number, and may participate in only one Aggregation at a time. FERC found the 10 kW minimum just and reasonable on April 15 2024 and confirmed it is not a temporary measure
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 and 4.1.10.1; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual)
market.stack: Resources under 10 kW remain eligible for EDRP, the SCR program (including Small Customer Aggregation) and NY State and utility DER programs

market.n: Energy Storage Resource (ESR) and Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) participation models
market.struct: Full participation in Energy, Ancillary Services and Installed Capacity markets as a standalone ESR, or as a Single Resource Type Aggregation of ESRs
market.limits: NYISO was the first ISO/RTO to allow full ESR participation in energy, capacity and ancillary services markets, implemented under FERC Order No. 841 (FERC accepted NYISO's Order 841 compliance revisions December 20 2019; full-participation model went live in 2020). Minimum size for wholesale participation as an ESR is 100 kW. A Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) is a regulation-focused model and must bid ISO-Committed-Flexible; an ESR may bid ISO-Committed-Flexible or Self-Committed Fixed/Flexible. Capacity market eligibility extends to resources able to store as little as two hours of energy, with time-stacking applied to resources with an Energy Duration Limitation (EDL). ESRs may withdraw (charge) at retail rates under Services Tariff 7.2.8
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 7.2.8 and 15.4.1.2.4; ICAP Manual Attachment J; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.1.3
market.export: Injections settled at Transmission Node LBMP; charging may be at wholesale LBMP or at the applicable retail rate
market.stack: Energy arbitrage + Regulation + Operating Reserves + ICAP from the same ESR; ESR-only Single Resource Type Aggregation; heterogeneous DER Aggregation with solar and demand response

market.n: Regulation Service (Regulation Capacity and Regulation Movement)
market.struct: $/MWh Regulation Capacity clearing price plus $/MW Regulation Movement payment for AGC following
market.limits: Reachable by a BTM resource two ways: (1) as a Demand Side Resource in the DSASP program (minimum 1 MW in aggregate by Load Zone; only interruptible load qualifies for Regulation - load backed by a Local Generator does not); or (2) inside a NYISO Aggregation, where under current pre-Order-2222 rules EVERY individual DER in the Aggregation must itself be capable of providing Regulation, and the Aggregation must bid self-committed flexible. Requires 6-second AGC base point following and 6-second two-way telemetry. A Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) is the regulation-oriented storage model and bids ISO-Committed-Flexible. Clearing prices not captured here - see NYISO Ancillary Services market data
market.tariff: Services Tariff Rate Schedule 3 and Section 15.4.1.2.4; Ancillary Services Manual; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.2.4
market.stack: Regulation + Energy + ICAP from the same resource; DSASP may be combined with SCR or EDRP but SCR/EDRP energy payments are netted against DSASP payments

market.n: Operating Reserves (10-Minute Spinning, 10-Minute Non-Synchronized, 30-Minute Synchronized, 30-Minute Non-Synchronized)
market.struct: $/MWh marginal clearing price by product and by reserve region
market.limits: Four Operating Reserve products. Reachable by a BTM resource via DSASP (minimum 1 MW in aggregate by Load Zone; only interruptible load may supply Spinning Reserve, while load served by a qualified Local Generator may supply Non-Synchronized Reserves) or via an Aggregation. Under current rules an Aggregation may only offer the product that EVERY member DER can supply - an aggregation of one 10-minute-spin facility plus two 30-minute-non-sync facilities can only offer 30-minute non-synchronized reserve. Aggregations must bid self-committed flexible; self-committed fixed and ISO-committed fixed bid modes are ineligible for reserves. New reserve Aggregations verify performance during the first two weeks of the first active month instead of prequalifying. DSASP resources must follow 5-minute RTD base points. Reserve prices differ by region (NYCA, East, SENY, Long Island); clearing prices not captured here
market.tariff: Services Tariff Rate Schedule 4 and Section 15.4.1.2.4; Ancillary Services Manual Section 6.12.2; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.2.4
market.stack: Reserves + Energy + ICAP from the same Aggregation; the all-members-capable restriction is scheduled to change under NYISO's Order 2222 implementation

market.n: Capacity Accreditation Factors (CAF) and Peak Load Window - 2025/2026 Capability Year
market.struct: Derating multiplier applied to ICAP before UCAP is sold; UCAP = ICAP x CAF x derating factor
market.val: 2025-2026 Final CAFs by Capacity Accreditation Resource Class (Rest of State / GHI Region / NYC Locality / LI Locality): Special Case Resource 77.21% / 76.88% / 68.31% / 74.43%. 2-Hour Energy Duration Limited 74.32% / 73.97% / 64.94% / 52.68%. 4-Hour EDL 78.91% / 78.60% / 78.53% / 87.10%. 6-Hour EDL 87.24% / 87.16% / 85.90% / 94.59%. 8-Hour EDL 96.77% / 96.40% / 96.12% / 98.96%. Solar 12.24% / 12.33% / 12.03% / 10.05%. Landfill Gas 63.95% / 63.87% / 64.04% / 65.68%. Generator and Large Hydro 100% in all regions
market.limits: Basis: 2025-2026 IRM 24.4%; G-J LCR 78.8%, Zone J LCR 78.5%, Zone K LCR 106.5%; LOLE 0.100 event-days/year. 2025-2026 Peak Load Window: Summer 10 hours HB 12 through HB 21; Winter 6 hours HB 16 through HB 21. The Peak Load Window sets the bid/schedule/notify obligation for DER, ESRs and resources with Energy Duration Limitations and feeds their derating factors. Optimal output window for SCRs is HB 17-20 (HB 16-19 in Load Zone K); for 4-hour EDL it is HB 16-18 and HB 20. Final CAFs must be posted on or before March 1 for the coming Capability Year
market.tariff: ICAP Manual Sections 7.3, 7.3.2, 7.3.3; ICAP Manual Attachment J
market.stack: Applies to SCR capacity revenue and to DER Aggregation ICAP revenue alike

market.n: Monthly Net Benefit Threshold (MNBT) - Order 745 net benefits test
market.struct: Price floor that gates energy payments for Demand Reductions
market.limits: NYISO runs the Net Benefits Test monthly and posts the Monthly Net Benefit Threshold by the 15th of the preceding month on its Demand Response page. A DER Aggregation or DADRP resource may OFFER below the MNBT, but Demand Reductions performed in an interval where the applicable Transmission Node LBMP is below the MNBT earn no Energy payment, no Day-Ahead Margin Assurance Payment and no Bid Production Cost Guarantee. Exception: if NYISO or the Transmission Owner dispatches the Aggregation for NYCA or local system reliability, the Demand Reductions remain eligible. A DER Aggregation also may not balance Energy withdrawals by Withdrawal-Eligible Generators against Demand Reductions in a Real-Time interval when the Transmission Node LBMP is below the MNBT. Current monthly values not captured here - they change every month
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 4.4.1.2, 4.5.2, 4.5.2.1, 4.5.7 and 4.5.7.1; Technical Bulletin 245; NYISO Manual 38 Section 2.1.3.2
market.stack: Gates DADRP and DER Aggregation demand-reduction energy revenue; does not affect capacity or ancillary services revenue

market.n: Co-located Storage Resource (CSR) participation model
market.struct: Energy, ancillary services and ICAP revenue for a storage resource sharing a point of injection with a co-located wind or solar resource
market.limits: FERC accepted NYISO's Co-located Storage Resource participation model on March 30 2021, covering Energy and Ancillary Services market rules, metering rules, the Interconnection Process, ICAP market participation rules and market power mitigation, for an ESR that shares a common point of injection with a wind or solar resource. Distinct from the Aggregation model - within an Aggregation, a facility with two or more technology types behind a single point of interconnection is treated as one DER with a maximum Injection Limit of 20 MW
market.tariff: NYISO Services Tariff and OATT CSR provisions
market.stack: Pairs with the ESR participation model; a co-located solar+storage facility may alternatively enroll as a single DER facility inside an Aggregation

market.n: Energy market price levels - 2025 average real-time LBMP by zone
market.struct: Reference price level for BTM energy arbitrage and demand-reduction revenue
market.val: 2025 calendar-year average real-time LBMP ranged from $54.40/MWh in the West Zone to $81/MWh on Long Island, the spread driven by transmission congestion and losses. RGGI CO2 allowance prices averaged nearly $23/ton in 2025, contributing more than $10/MWh (about 28 percent of production cost) for a typical Central Zone combined cycle
market.limits: NYISO reserve shortage prices reach $750 to $3,000/MWh even in deep shortages, materially below ISO-NE and PJM ($4,000 to $12,000/MWh), which caps the upside of scarcity-driven BTM dispatch in New York. TSA-related congestion in high-risk hours averaged $300 to $500/MWh in 2025
market.rates: Zonal spread West $54.40/MWh to Long Island $81/MWh in 2025
market.export: Settled at Transmission Node LBMP for Aggregations
market.stack: Energy arbitrage stacks with ICAP and ancillary services

market.n: SCR to DER Participation Model transition rules
market.struct: No payment - switching rule between the two capacity-earning DR pathways
market.limits: An active SCR may move to the DER participation model monthly: the SCR must be separated in DRIS before the close of the Certification period for the auction month preceding the intended first DER month. A transitioning SCR may use a Provisional DMNC capped at the upper limit of Installed Capacity calculated for the SCR (its former Average Coincident Load) for the immediately prior like Capability Period, submitted within the first 7 days of the pending-review month; the Provisional DMNC must later be validated by an in-period DMNC test and the Aggregation is exposed to oversold-capacity penalties. Moving the other way is much slower: a DER whose capability contributed to an Aggregation's UCAP must give notice by August 1 and can only rejoin the SCR program the following May 1. An SCR base performance test cannot substitute for a DMNC test. As of June 2025 the MMU reported only ONE demand response resource had actually transitioned from SCR to DER
market.tariff: Services Tariff Sections 5.12.11.1, 5.12.11.1.1 and 5.12.13.1; NYISO Manual 38 Sections 2.2.5 and 4.3.3
market.stack: Mutually exclusive with SCR - a resource cannot be both an SCR and a DER at the same time

market.n: Distributed Energy Resource Provider (DERP) - Distributed Energy Resource Aggregation (DERA), energy and ancillary services
market.struct: $/MWh Day-Ahead and Real-Time LMP at the aggregation's PNode(s) (weighted by Generation Distribution Factors) plus $/MW ancillary service capacity awards; settled as a single supply resource
market.limits: Aggregation minimum 100 kW (reduced from 0.5 MW under Order 2222; validated as aggregate Pmax >= 0.1 MW); individual DERs must be under 1 MW (a generating unit of 1 MW or more in the CAISO BAA must become a Participating Generator instead); aggregation spanning multiple PNodes capped at 20 MW; all DERs must sit in ONE Sub-LAP; a DER may be in only one DERA and may not also participate in the CAISO market separately. Modeled as a generic Non-Generating Resource, non-REM subtype. Requires a DERP Agreement (Tariff Appendix B.21), a certified Scheduling Coordinator with a Meter Service Agreement for SCs (SC Metered Entity, SQMD submitted daily for all intervals), a 30-business-day UDC/MSS concurrence review before New Resource Implementation, and UDC interconnection (Rule 21 / WDT) approval. Telemetry: not required for energy-only unless 10 MW or greater; required at any size for Spin/Non-Spin (4-second status). Aggregated response at each PNode must move in the direction of the dispatch
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Section 4.17 (4.17.3 Requirements, 4.17.4 UDC review, 4.17.5 Characteristics, 4.17.6 Operating Requirements) and Appendix B.21 (DERP Agreement); Appendix K ASRP A.1.1/B.1.1/C.1.1; BPM for Generator Management; BPM for Market Instruments; BPM for Direct Telemetry
market.export: Net injections settled at PNode LMP (GDF-weighted); charging settled as negative supply
market.stack: Energy + Spinning + Non-Spinning Reserve from the same DERA. NOT eligible to provide Resource Adequacy per CAISO's PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA comparison matrix (Nov 2023). A DER in a DERA may not also be in another DERA, may not bid separately, and may not be on a retail NEM program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation (Tariff 4.17.3). Seven entities hold DERP Agreements (3rd Rock Systems, Apparent Energy, Galt Power, Olivine, SDG&E, Shell Energy North America, Silicon Valley Clean Energy)

market.n: Heterogeneous DER Aggregation (HDERA) with Distributed Curtailment Resources - FERC Order 2222 model
market.struct: $/MWh LMP on the SUM of net DER energy injection plus DCR demand curtailment (curtailment metered as positive supply); settled as one generic NGR non-REM resource
market.limits: Live since November 1 2024 (Tariff 4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6). Must contain at least one Distributed Curtailment Resource (demand response) and may also contain injecting DERs. Minimum 100 kW aggregate Pmax. All locations in the same Sub-LAP; PNodes Pre-Defined (default GDFs) or Customized (DERP-specified GDFs summing to 1); GDFs may be resubmitted with hourly bids. Bids are subject to the same Net Benefits Test price threshold as PDR. DCR curtailment is measured against an ISO-approved baseline from Tariff 4.13.4 (weather matching, control group, day-matching 10-in-10 / 5-in-10 residential / combined, Meter Generator Output variants, EVSE residential/non-residential variants, PDR-LSR variants). SCME must submit net DER energy, DCR curtailment, the baseline used, and underlying hourly consumption for all baseline days. Any change to locations, capacity, baseline or SC requires a new UDC concurrence (Attachment A) submission
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Sections 4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6, 4.13.4; FERC Order 2222 Business Requirements Specification v1.2 (Jun 28 2024) BRQ-002, BRQ-005, BRQ-008, BRQ-009, BRQ-106; BPM for Demand Response Section 5 (baselines)
market.export: Net DER injection + DCR curtailment both settled at PNode LMP
market.stack: Energy + Spin/Non-Spin as for DERA. Same double-counting guard as DERA: DER on a retail NEM program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation is barred; UDC may raise double-counting concerns in its review

market.n: FERC Order 2222 implementation status - CAISO DER Aggregation
market.struct: Rule / timeline row - no direct payment
market.limits: COMPLETE. CAISO has had a DERP/DERA model since 2016 (tariff 4.17 as of Jun 3 2016; minimum 0.5 MW). Order 2222 compliance filed July 19 2021 (amended Nov 1 2021); FERC accepted it June 17 2022 (179 FERC 61197), most revisions effective June 16 2022 (incl. 100 kW minimum, small-utility opt-in, NEM double-count guard, revised DER definition). Second compliance filing Aug 15 2022 (amended Jan 10 2023) accepted May 18 2023 (183 FERC 61119) with the heterogeneous DERA / Distributed Curtailment Resource provisions deferred to no later than Nov 1 2024. CAISO implemented them November 1 2024 and filed an informational filing Nov 5 2024 stating this completes its Order 2222 compliance. CAISO was the first RTO/ISO to finish
market.tariff: FERC Docket ER21-2455; CAISO Tariff Sections 4.17.3-4.17.7, 11.6.5.1, 30.5.2.6, Appendix B.21, Appendix K
market.stack: Applies to DERA and HDERA; does not change PDR/RDRR rules

market.n: Small utility opt-in gate and state aggregation rules for DER Aggregations
market.struct: Eligibility gate - no payment
market.limits: California has NOT opted out of third-party aggregation of retail customers; CPUC has permitted third-party Demand Response Providers to bid retail customers into CAISO as PDR since the DR direct-participation rules (Electric Rule 24 at PG&E/SCE, Rule 32 at SDG&E). The only Order 2222 gate is the small-utility provision: CAISO may not accept a DERA containing customers of a utility that distributed 4 million MWh or less in the prior fiscal year unless that utility's RERRA permits it (DERP Agreement Appendix B.21 Section 4.1.4; the same opt-in already existed in the pro forma Demand Response Provider Agreement). In practice this reaches small California publicly owned utilities and MSS operators inside the CAISO BAA. Separately a DER on a retail net energy metering program that does not expressly permit wholesale participation is barred from a DERA
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Appendix B.21 Section 4.1.4 (Small Utility Limits); Tariff Section 4.17.3; FERC 183 FERC 61119 (May 18 2023) at P 5
market.stack: Customers of PG&E, SCE and SDG&E face no opt-in gate

market.n: Proxy Demand Resource (PDR) - energy
market.struct: $/MWh Day-Ahead and Real-Time LMP (at a proxy-generator PNode or GDF-weighted Sub-LAP aggregation) on Demand Response Energy Measurement = Customer Baseline minus actual load; paid only when bids clear at or above the monthly Net Benefits Test price threshold
market.val: DMM-reported 2024 net energy market revenue per MWh delivered (RA-counted PDR): utility PDR about $144/MWh, third-party PDR about $48/MWh; per kW-year: utility PDR $1.59, third-party PDR $2.67 (2024), down from $26.97 and $15.18 (2022). Real-time soft offer cap $1,000/MWh (hard cap $2,000/MWh under stressed conditions); CPUC caps non-DRAM RA PDR bids at $949/MWh from 2024 (D.23-06-029)
market.limits: Minimum 100 kW curtailment for energy, sustainable for bid duration; must bid at or above the Net Benefits Test threshold price (Tariff 30.6.3, posted monthly); Day-Ahead and Real-Time energy; real-time bid dispatch option 60, 15 or 5 minutes (default 60; hourly-block option not eligible for energy bid cost recovery); all locations under one LSE and one Sub-LAP per registration (resource may span LSEs per comparison matrix); Demand Response Provider Agreement plus a certified SC; LSE and UDC 10-day location review in DRRS; outages only as 0 MW (all-or-nothing) PMax derates; telemetry not required for energy unless Pmax 10 MW or greater; statistical sampling permitted where interval metering is incomplete (min sample 271/(N+271)). Baselines: 10-in-10 (adj. cap 80-120%), 5-in-10 residential (71-140%), weather matching, control group (>=150 end users), Meter Generator Output (MGO) and combinations, EVSE
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Sections 4.13, 4.13.4 (baselines), 11.6, 30.6.3 (NBT), Appendix B (DRPA); BPM for Demand Response Sections 2, 5, 7, 11, 15, 16
market.export: No export credit - net export intervals set to zero
market.stack: Stacks with PDR Spin/Non-Spin and with RA (NQC). NEM locations may join, but any interval with net export at a location is set to zero under Customer Load Baseline methods; under MGO the storage/generator output counts only up to on-site demand and is zeroed while charging - so a PDR battery earns for offsetting on-site load, NOT for export. CPUC-jurisdictional double-counting rules (e.g. no simultaneous enrollment in utility DR programs for the same load) apply via the UDC/LSE review

market.n: Proxy Demand Resource - Load Shift Resource (PDR-LSR)
market.struct: Two resource IDs: Curtailment (CUR) paid $/MWh LMP for load reduction/discharge like a PDR; Consumption (CON) bids from the bid floor up to below $0/MWh and is paid (negative LMP) for increasing load (charging) during oversupply
market.limits: Registered location(s) must include at least one behind-the-meter storage device (sub-metered). Must bid real-time in 5- or 15-minute intervals only (no hourly option); both IDs registered on the same GRDT with the same bid option, SC and effective dates. CUR ID: FUEL_TYPE GEN, eligible for RA and Spin/Non-Spin, must bid at or above the NBT threshold, non-export rules apply. CON ID: modeled like an NGR Dispatchable Demand Resource (MIN_GEN<0, MAX_GEN=0), ineligible for RA and ancillary services, bid must be below $0. Performance: storage-only configuration, or facility-load CLB plus storage (PDR-LSR with 5-in-10, 10-in-10, combined, or weather-matching)
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Sections 4.13.4.7 and 11.6.7; BPM for Demand Response Sections 2, 5.7, 7, 8, 16
market.export: No export credit - curtailment side uses non-export rules
market.stack: The CUR side stacks with RA and Spin/Non-Spin; the CON side is energy-only. Charging credit only when the CON resource is dispatched at negative prices; ordinary retail-rate charging is not credited

market.n: Proxy Demand Resource (PDR) - Spinning and Non-Spinning Reserve
market.struct: $/MW-hour ancillary service capacity award (Day-Ahead and Real-Time Spin / Non-Spin marginal prices) plus energy if dispatched
market.limits: Minimum 500 kW curtailment, sustainable 30 minutes for Spin/Non-Spin awards; requires Ancillary Service certification and direct telemetry at ANY size (4-second status, 60-second update, 1-minute scan per Direct Telemetry BPM); PDR must submit load meter data for the interval before, during and after awarded intervals; No-Pay charge rescinds reserve capacity payment if the resource does not perform. PDR cannot provide Regulation. Statistical sampling allowed for RT/AS only when all locations have interval meters
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Section 8 and Appendix K (ASRP); BPM for Demand Response Sections 2, 11, 12; BPM for Direct Telemetry
market.stack: Stacks with PDR energy and RA; PDR-LSR Consumption ID is ineligible

market.n: Reliability Demand Response Resource (RDRR)
market.struct: $/MWh LMP on Demand Response Energy Measurement; primary value is RA credit to the load-serving entity
market.val: DMM 2024: utility RDRR net energy market revenue about $46/MWh delivered, about $0.41/kW-year (2024), vs $3.42/kW-year (2022)
market.limits: Minimum 500 kW load reduction per RDRR; reach full curtailment within 40 minutes of dispatch; sustain at least 4 consecutive hours per event; minimum run time no more than 1 hour; discrete dispatch option capped at 100 MW (exception by attestation), marginal option uncapped; dispatch option selected once per season (summer Jun-Sep, winter Oct-May). May bid economically in Day-Ahead; real-time incremental bids must be at least 95% of the energy bid cap (e.g. $950 at a $1,000 cap; $1,900 at $2,000) and can only be dispatched in real time under an Energy Emergency Alert Watch or higher (since 2023 per CPUC D.23-06-029; previously EEA 2). Cannot offer Ancillary Services or RUC. Primarily utility Base Interruptible Program and agricultural pumping loads
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Section 4.13; BPM for Demand Response Sections 2 and 7; CAISO Operating Procedure 4420
market.stack: RA (credited against IOU obligations). Not stackable with AS. Accessible to BTM customers mainly by enrolling in a utility emergency program (e.g. BIP) rather than directly

market.n: Demand Response Auction Mechanism (DRAM) - CPUC pilot, third-party PDR/RDRR capacity contracts with PG&E, SCE, SDG&E
market.struct: Pay-as-bid $/kW-month RA capacity contract paid by the IOU (performance-banded) plus CAISO energy payments to the third-party DRP when its PDR/RDRR is dispatched
market.val: 2024 (final year) authorized pilot budgets: PG&E $6,000,000; SCE $6,000,000; SDG&E $2,000,000 (D.23-01-006). Contract prices were confidential; not published
market.limits: SUNSET. CPUC D.24-04-006 (Apr 18 2024) ended the DRAM pilots of PG&E, SCE and SDG&E by December 31 2024 (or earlier if 2024 funding was exhausted); IOUs may process invoices through 2025 and true up in 2026 Annual Electric True-Up advice letters. No 2025+ DRAM deliveries. Reasons found: Nexant evaluation showed at most 3 of 6 criteria met; failed reliability and cost-competitiveness; bids at or near the CAISO price cap; demonstrated capacity 57% of contracted in 2021; 2024 solicitation offered only 73.05 MW vs 200+ MW/yr in 2018-2021
market.stack: Was a wrapper around CAISO PDR/RDRR (energy paid by CAISO, RA capacity paid by IOU). CPUC-named successor pathways for third-party DRPs: PG&E and SCE Capacity Bidding Program Elect, SDG&E CBP, IOU and CCA RA solicitations (bilateral), and CEC Demand Side Grid Support (DSGS). Customers remain free to be bid into CAISO as PDR by a third party - only the IOU-funded capacity contract ended

market.n: Resource Adequacy (RA) pathway for demand response - PDR/RDRR shown on LSE Supply Plans under the CPUC Slice-of-Day framework
market.struct: No CAISO capacity payment and no CAISO capacity auction. Value is a bilateral $/kW-month RA contract with a California LSE (IOU, CCA, ESP) or an IOU DR program (e.g. Capacity Bidding Program) that counts the PDR/RDRR toward the LSE's CPUC RA obligation
market.limits: CAISO side (BPM for Reliability Requirements Sections 7.1.1-7.1.2 as summarized in CAISO PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA matrix): System RA must-offer obligation - a PDR must bid whenever it has demand-reduction availability (24 h/day if capable); minimum DR MOO capability of 4 hours per dispatch, 3 consecutive days of dispatch, and 24 hours per month; PDR bids are not subject to local market power mitigation. Flexible RA: DR fits Use-Limited Super-Peak Ramping (MOO May-Sep 7am-12pm per matrix text, Oct-Apr 3-8pm; non-holiday weekdays; min 3 hours at EFC; at least 5 dispatches/month). CPUC side (2025 RA and Slice-of-Day Guide; D.23-04-010, D.23-06-029, D.24-06-004): DR shown for four consecutive hours of the Availability Assessment Hour window (or the full AAH window if contract/tariff requires longer dispatch); hourly value = capability on the worst day of the month under a 1-in-2 framework from ex ante Load Impact Protocol results; TLF and PRM adders removed, distribution loss factor adder retained; DR MCC bucket limit 8.3% of each slice; 17% PRM for 2025. Supply-side DR and storage may not be used to cover the LSE's storage-charging sufficiency requirement. RA NQC for DR must be re-authorized by the Local Regulatory Authority from the latest LIP before it is placed on CAISO's NQC list
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Section 40 (RA), 40.10.3.2-40.10.3.4 (flexible categories); BPM for Reliability Requirements Sections 7.1.1, 7.1.2; CPUC D.23-04-010, D.23-06-029 (OP 29), D.24-06-004; CPUC 2025 RA and Slice of Day Filing Guide Section 7
market.stack: RA-shown PDR and RDRR still earn CAISO energy (and PDR Spin/Non-Spin) revenues. The DERA/HDERA (DERP) model is INELIGIBLE to provide RA per the CAISO comparison matrix, so a BTM battery aggregation seeking RA value must register as PDR/PDR-LSR (CUR side only), not as a DERA. PDR-LSR Consumption ID is ineligible for RA. DRAM (IOU-funded RA contracts for third-party DR) ended Dec 31 2024

market.n: Ancillary Services (Regulation Up/Down, Spinning Reserve, Non-Spinning Reserve) - reachability for BTM aggregations and DMM clearing prices
market.struct: $/MW-hour capacity payment at the Day-Ahead ancillary service market clearing price; Real-Time pays only incremental capacity above the DA award; rescinded (No-Pay) if the resource does not perform
market.val: DMM quantity-weighted average clearing prices ($/MW per hour), 2024 -> 2025. Day-Ahead: Reg Up $4.37 -> $3.40; Reg Down $6.29 -> $7.51; Spin $4.18 -> $0.84; Non-Spin $1.96 -> $0.94. Real-Time: Reg Up $7.18 -> $10.14; Reg Down $7.15 -> $16.18; Spin $1.03 -> $0.80; Non-Spin $0.85 -> $0.85. About 90% of 2025 AS cost was incurred day-ahead. Total CAISO AS cost $94.5M in 2025 ($0.47/MWh of load). DMM: actual CAISO batteries earned about $9/kW-yr from regulation in 2025; batteries supplied 53% of AS requirements
market.limits: Which BTM participation models can reach which product (CAISO PDR-DERP-NGR-LFA comparison matrix): PDR - Spin and Non-Spin only (500 kW minimum curtailment sustainable 30 min; direct telemetry at any size); DERA/HDERA - Energy plus Spin and Non-Spin (modeled as generic NGR, NON-REM subtype per Order 2222 BRS BRQ-002; direct telemetry required at any size for AS); REGULATION UP/DOWN is listed only for the Non-Generator Resource (NGR) model (LESR/DDR subtypes; 500 kW minimum; 4-second telemetry with 8-second round trip; 60-min continuous energy non-REM or 15-min under REM), which requires the ISO interconnection and New Resource Implementation process and ISO- or SC-metering of the resource - i.e. not a retail-meter BTM aggregation path. RDRR and the PDR-LSR Consumption ID cannot provide any AS. All AS requires AS certification (Tariff Appendix K) and unannounced compliance testing (7% of resources failed in 2025)
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Section 8 and Appendix K (Ancillary Service Requirements Protocol); Tariff 4.17.7; BPM for Market Instruments Section 3.2; BPM for Direct Telemetry; DMM 2025 Annual Report on Market Issues and Performance Chapter 12 (Figures 12.4 and 12.5)
market.stack: Co-optimized with energy for the same resource. BTM battery aggregations realistically reach Spin/Non-Spin (via PDR or DERA) but not Regulation; Regulation needs a wholesale-metered NGR. RA-shown PDR can also sell Spin/Non-Spin

market.n: WEIM / EDAM - access for customer-sited batteries in non-CAISO California balancing areas (LADWP, BANC/SMUD, TID, IID)
market.struct: No direct CAISO payment to the customer or a third-party aggregator. In WEIM, demand response enters only as a Load Forecast Adjustment submitted by the WEIM Entity (the utility/BA) - implicitly valued as a self-schedule; the BA, not the DR provider, sees any real-time imbalance settlement
market.limits: Answer: effectively NO direct path. The CAISO retail-DR and DER aggregation models (PDR, PDR-LSR, RDRR, DERA/HDERA) are CAISO-balancing-area participation models. In a WEIM BAA the only CAISO-recognized DR mechanism is the WEIM Entity's Load Forecast Adjustment (no minimum size; aggregated across forecast zones within the WEIM BAA; 5-minute schedule submitted a day ahead and updated to T-45; WEIM Entity must sign a DR attestation per EIM BPM Appendix C; no telemetry requirement). A BTM battery can only reach WEIM value indirectly through the host utility's own DR/VPP program. Status of the host BAs: TID has been a WEIM participant since 2021; LADWP and BANC (incl. SMUD) are WEIM participants and signed EDAM implementation agreements (BANC Nov 22 2024; LADWP Jan 13 2025) for planned EDAM entry in 2027; TID signed May 19 2025 for 2027; IID signed May 22 2025 for 2028. EDAM went live May 1 2026 with PacifiCorp (PGE planned 2026). CAISO matrix notes a day-ahead LFA option pending EDAM tariff approval
market.tariff: CAISO Tariff Section 29 (WEIM), 29.34 (WEIM Entity load forecast / DR); EDAM Tariff Section 33; BPM for Energy Imbalance Market Appendix C (Demand Response Attestation); EDAM Implementation Agreements for BANC, LADWP, TID, IID
market.stack: Only via the POU's own retail program (e.g. SMUD, LADWP, TID DR/VPP programs), which is outside CAISO. FERC Order 2222 DER aggregation rights attach to RTO/ISO balancing areas and do not reach these public-power BAs

MN.rule_citation: Minn. Stat. 216B.164; Minn. Rules ch. 7835 (7835.4013-4015); MN Distributed Interconnection Process (MN DIP) and Technical Interconnection and Interoperability Requirements (TIIR), Docket E999/CI-16-521
MN.applies_to: All utilities (IOU + co-op + muni; compensation mechanics differ by ownership type)
MN.nem_successor: No mandatory statewide successor for rooftop NEM; Xcel Value of Solar (VOS) tariff is optional alternative for Xcel residential/small customers and became mandatory for new Xcel community solar garden (CSG) subscribers under a phased ARR-to-VOS transition effective April 1 2025 (Docket E002/M-21-694)
MN.nem_sizing_rule: <=120% of prior 12-month (or projected) on-site consumption combined with any community solar garden subscription (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.4c; 216B.1641)
MN.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (Average Retail Utility Energy Rate, systems <40 kW AC); avoided-cost/simultaneous purchase-and-sale rate or time-of-day rate for 40kW-1MW; value-of-DER stack (VOS) optional for Xcel, mandatory for new Xcel CSG subscribers
MN.export_credit_value: Average Retail Utility Energy Rate set annually per utility, varies by utility (statewide average roughly $0.12-0.14/kWh); Xcel VOS approx. $0.1909/kWh for CSG subscribers as filed 2025, stepping down for C&I subscribers (~$0.13/kWh 2025, ~$0.12/kWh 2026)
MN.credit_rollover: Monthly netting under 40kW; annual banking option for 40kW-1MW systems
MN.annual_true_up: Excess annual banked credits for public-utility customers cashed out at avoided cost; co-op/muni excess credits canceled with no payment (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.3a and Subd.3(f))
MN.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SA/SB (Minnesota was first state to adopt IEEE 1547-2018 statewide via TIIR, Commission order Jan 22 2020; docket E999/CI-16-521 remains open for Phase II refinements)
MN.ic_application_fee: Simplified process: $100 + $1/kWac; Study process: $1000 + $2/kWac; statewide $30 surcharge added to all applications
MN.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (typically required for larger/study-track systems; often waived for UL1741-SB inverter-based systems under simplified process — confirm per utility)
MN.insurance_required: Not specified in statewide rule; utility-specific in interconnection agreement
MN.ic_timeline_days: ic_timeline_days not specified as single statewide statutory number in sources reviewed; MN DIP sets tiered review deadlines by track (see MN DIP document)
MN.non_export_option: Yes — defined non-export operating mode exists (MN DIP Exhibit B for Energy Storage; Xcel Energy MN Electric Energy Storage Interconnection Guidelines) using control-system settings and bi-directional metering to enforce zero export
MN.storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes (storage nameplate/inverter capacity at point of interconnection generally counts toward system size for NEM/DIP purposes; confirm per utility tariff)
MN.standby_charge: Not specified in statewide statute; co-op/muni may impose DG fixed-cost recovery fee (Minn. Stat. 216B.164 Subd.3(a)); public utilities barred from DG-specific fixed fees beyond standard retail fixed charges

WI.rule_citation: Wis. Admin. Code PSC 119 (interconnection); no statewide net metering statute — parallel generation buyback rates set utility-by-utility via individual tariff dockets
WI.applies_to: IOU + co-op + muni (PSC 119 interconnection technical rules apply to all DG facilities <=15 MW seeking interconnection to a utility distribution system; buyback/compensation tariffs are NOT statewide and are set per-utility)
WI.nem_successor: No formal statewide NEM successor; each utility runs its own parallel-generation buyback tariff. PSC reopened a statewide Net Energy Metering investigation (2023-2025) and commissioned a Value of Solar Study (VOSS) literature review with Berkeley Lab/national labs; as of the Sept 2024 open meeting the Commission had taken no policy action and was awaiting the VOSS literature review — docket remains open and outcome could reset buyback rates statewide within the next 1-2 years
WI.nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap (varies by utility tariff)
WI.nem_sizing_rule: Not standardized statewide; individual utility tariffs may impose sizing limits tied to historical usage
WI.export_credit_basis: Buy-all-sell-all / avoided-cost buyback rate for excess above NEM threshold, set per-utility tariff (not 1:1 retail beyond the NEM threshold in most IOU territories)
WI.export_credit_value: Varies sharply by utility — e.g. We Energies buyback ~$0.0317/kWh (2026); WPS/WPL retail-rate net metering up to 20 kW; see FILE 2 utility rows for utility-specific figures
WI.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + IEEE 1547.1-2020 incorporated by reference into PSC 119 (effective per PSC 119 rule revision)
WI.ic_application_fee: Not standardized statewide; varies by utility
WI.ic_study_trigger_kw: Not standardized statewide; varies by utility (larger/complex projects trigger supplemental review under PSC 119)
WI.ic_timeline_days: Not specified as single statewide statutory number; PSC 119 sets tiered review timelines by DG category
WI.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear (varies by utility; grid-charging treatment is not addressed uniformly in PSC 119 and is a live issue in the NEM/VOSS docket)
WI.non_export_option: Yes — PSC 119 defines a non-exporting Category 1 pathway for co-located storage no larger than 20 kW paired with a non-exporting DG resource no larger than 20 kW, which qualifies for simplified/expedited review
WI.storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes for exporting configurations (storage nameplate counts toward DG facility capacity category under PSC 119); non-exporting storage handled separately under Category 1
WI.standby_charge: Not specified in statewide rule; some utilities (e.g. We Energies) assess a Generation Customer Charge (~$0.059/day) on DG customers — utility-specific

IA.jurisdiction_body: Iowa Utilities Commission (formerly Iowa Utilities Board)
IA.rule_citation: Iowa Code 476.49 (SF 583, enacted 2020); 199 IAC Chapter 45 (interconnection technical standards)
IA.applies_to: IOU only for the codified SF 583 inflow-outflow regime (applies to rate-regulated utilities i.e. MidAmerican and Alliant/Interstate Power and Light); municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives are exempt from IUC rate/NEM jurisdiction and set their own net metering/DG policies
IA.nem_successor: SF 583 (2020) replaced true net metering with an inflow/outflow billing structure for new DG customers starting July 1 2020; MidAmerican tariff effective Nov 24 2020, Alliant/IPL tariff effective Dec 30 2020. Outflow rate initially set equal to the retail (inflow) rate but is scheduled to transition toward a value-of-solar-informed rate once the 5% statewide penetration trigger is reached or by 2027, whichever first — a Value of Solar study/proceeding is the anticipated successor mechanism and is not yet finalized as of last verification
IA.nem_aggregate_cap: 5% of each utility's statewide peak electric demand (statutory trigger for VOS proceeding; current subscription level not confirmed in sources reviewed)
IA.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail equivalent under inflow-outflow (outflow credited at same rate as inflow/retail rate, i.e. functionally 1:1 at present)
IA.export_credit_value: Outflow rate = retail rate as of 2020 tariffs (MidAmerican eff. 11/24/2020; Alliant/IPL eff. 12/30/2020); scheduled to move toward value-of-solar basis post-trigger — confirm current cents/kWh in utility tariff
IA.credit_rollover: Monthly billing under inflow-outflow (kWh-for-kWh at time of use within billing period; no long-term banking under strict inflow-outflow design — confirm)
IA.annual_true_up: Monthly per SF 583 inflow-outflow structure; no annual true-up mechanism identified in sources reviewed
IA.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 (incorporated into 199 IAC 45.3, effective per rule dated April 6 2018 edition; rule revision effective 7/16/2025 per Iowa Admin Code updates)
IA.ic_fast_track_kw: NEM/interconnection uses tiered Levels 1-4 application process (Level 1 = smallest/fastest per 199 IAC 45); exact kW threshold for Level 1 not confirmed in sources reviewed
IA.ic_simplified_kw: Not confirmed in sources reviewed for Level 2/3 thresholds
IA.ic_study_trigger_kw: Not confirmed in sources reviewed (Level 3/4 studies triggered for larger/more complex systems per 199 IAC 45)
IA.ic_timeline_days: Not confirmed in sources reviewed (tiered by Level under 199 IAC 45)
IA.non_export_option: Unclear — non-export pathway not confirmed in sources reviewed for 199 IAC Chapter 45; recommend direct rule review
IA.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear — not confirmed whether storage nameplate counts toward the 1 MW AC / 110%-of-usage sizing cap

ND.rule_citation: N.D. Admin. Code (net metering rule adopted 1991); no statewide interconnection procedures rule (confirmed by Freeing the Grid / IREC-Vote Solar 2026 scorecard: ND has not adopted statewide interconnection procedures)
ND.applies_to: IOU only (net metering rule applies only to investor-owned utility customers; municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives are NOT covered and set their own policies at their discretion)
ND.nem_successor: No formal statewide interconnection procedure exists; net-excess-generation purchase rule dates to 1991 and is thin — avoided-cost buyback only, not retail net metering. No successor tariff or active docket identified in sources reviewed
ND.export_credit_value: Not specified statewide; avoided cost is utility-specific and not published centrally
ND.credit_rollover: Monthly (net excess generation settled monthly at avoided cost per source reviewed)
ND.ic_standard: Not specified — no statewide interconnection technical standard identified; utilities individually reference IEEE 1547 in their own tariffs
ND.non_export_option: No statewide rule — utility discretion; no defined statewide non-export pathway identified

SD.rule_citation: S.D. Codified Laws 49-34A (utility service territory law); no statewide net metering statute or rule — PUC regulates small generator interconnection practice and mandates utilities purchase excess generation at avoided cost, but has explicitly declined to adopt net metering
SD.applies_to: IOU only for PUC-regulated interconnection/purchase obligation (municipal utilities and rural electric cooperatives largely outside PUC rate jurisdiction and set their own terms)
SD.nem_successor: No statewide rule — no successor because there was never a net metering program to succeed. PUC has published an explicit rationale (Compensation FAQ page) for why net metering has not been adopted; avoided-cost purchase obligation is the sole statewide mechanism, confirmed current as of Oct 10 2024 PUC Solar Energy FAQ
SD.export_credit_value: Avoided-cost rates are utility-specific and filed with/approved by the PUC for IOUs (publicly viewable at puc.sd.gov/energy/rrrates.aspx); no single statewide cents/kWh figure
SD.credit_rollover: Not specified — no banking/rollover mechanism under avoided-cost purchase
SD.ic_standard: Not specified — no statewide interconnection technical standard identified in sources reviewed; utilities individually reference IEEE 1547 in their own interconnection agreements
SD.non_export_option: No statewide rule — utility discretion; no defined statewide non-export pathway identified

MI.rule_citation: MCL 460.1173; PA 341/342 of 2016; PA 235 of 2023; Mich. Admin. Code R 460.901a-1026 (MIXDG rules, eff. 4/25/2023)
MI.applies_to: IOU + AES (member co-ops exempt but many voluntarily participate)
MI.nem_successor: Distributed Generation (DG) program under PA 341/342 replaced net metering for all new customers starting 2016-2019 (utility-specific transition dates); billed via separate inflow/outflow metering rather than net kWh. Legacy NEM customers grandfathered for 10 years from enrollment date, with storage additions permitted without loss of grandfathering per R 460.920(5)(m) if not a 'material modification'.
MI.nem_aggregate_cap: 10% of utility's average in-state peak load over preceding 5 years (raised from 1% by PA 235 of 2023, eff. 2023); allocated not less than 5% for <=20kW projects and not more than 5% for >20-550kW projects
MI.nem_sizing_rule: <=110% of customer's average annual electricity consumption (raised from 100% by PA 235)
MI.export_credit_basis: unbundled generation rate (LMP-based for DTE; utility-specific avoided-cost/power-supply component for others)
MI.export_credit_value: DTE Electric: outflow credited at monthly average real-time LMP at DTE load nodes, power-supply/PSCR component only, not delivery; Consumers Energy and other utility rates vary by tariff rider - see utility file
MI.credit_rollover: monthly netting of inflow/outflow (not indefinite rollover)
MI.annual_true_up: Excess outflow credited monthly at outflow rate; no annual banking of kWh as under retail NEM since inflow and outflow are billed as separate line items each month
MI.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SB (MIXDG rules eff. 4/25/2023; supersedes prior IEEE 1547-2003/UL1741-SA under rescinded net metering rules)
MI.ic_application_fee: $300 pre-application report cap; fast track initial review $100+$1/kWac (certified) or $100+$2/kWac (non-certified); fast track supplemental review cap $1000; non-export track $100+$1-2/kWac; legacy NEM/DG program app fee combined with fast-track fees capped at $50 total (R 460.926)
MI.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not explicitly mandated statewide in MIXDG rules; determined by utility interconnection procedures per R 460.920)
MI.insurance_required: Not specified in state rule; utility-specific
MI.ic_timeline_days: Level 1/2/3 use statewide standard agreement; commission order deadlines are 360 days for utility to file procedures, per-application timelines set in utility-approved procedures (R 460.920)
MI.non_export_option: Yes - explicit rule-based non-export/limited-export path via R 460.980: reverse power relay (0.1% export default), under-power relay, small-DER-vs-load exemption (<=50% of min host load), reduced output setting, or NRTL-certified power control system with 2-second trip on inadvertent export >30s
MI.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - not explicitly addressed in DG program rules reviewed; battery kW is not separately capped from PV kW under the 550kW system cap
MI.standby_charge: Not identified in rules reviewed for residential/small C&I; utilities may petition for utility-specific standby/facility charges via general rate case

IN.applies_to: IOU only (municipal and REMC/cooperative utilities largely exempt and set own rules)
IN.nem_successor: SEA 309 (2017, IC 8-1-40) closed 1:1 retail-rate net metering to new customers effective for IOU customers who did not enroll by a utility-specific 2017-2022 cutoff (approx. mid-2022 for most IOUs, per 30-month transition after 2018 enactment cutoff). Successor is the Excess Distributed Generation (EDG) tariff: excess (outflow) energy credited at 125% of the utility's prior-calendar-year average marginal/wholesale price of energy (IC 8-1-40-17), typically ~3-5 cents/kWh vs 14-17 cents/kWh retail. Grandfathering: systems installed/enrolled before 2018 retain full 1:1 net metering until July 1, 2047; systems enrolled between 2018 and the utility's net-metering closure date (the '2022 cohort') retain full net metering until July 1, 2032. After the respective sunset date, grandfathered customers move to the EDG rate.
IN.nem_aggregate_cap: Not specified as a statewide numeric aggregate cap under SEA 309 (unlike MI's 10% cap structure) - EDG is open-ended/uncapped by kW as a matter of state law; utility-specific queue/study limits may apply
IN.nem_sizing_rule: Generator nameplate capacity limited to the lesser of 1 MW or customer's average annual electricity consumption at the premises
IN.export_credit_value: 125% of the utility's average marginal/wholesale energy price for the prior calendar year (IC 8-1-40-17); e.g. AES Indiana 3.9350 cents/kWh effective 7/1/2024, updated annually via March 1 compliance filing - see utility file for other IOUs
IN.credit_rollover: indefinite (EDG credit balance carries forward indefinitely while customer remains on the rider; forfeited to FAC upon account closure)
IN.annual_true_up: No fixed annual true-up date under EDG; credit accumulates indefinitely as a running balance offsetting future bills down to the minimum charge
IN.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (referenced generally; UL 1741 as certification basis - 2018 edition transition referenced in pending 170 IAC 4-4.3 rule revisions not yet confirmed finalized)
IN.ic_application_fee: Not specified as a statewide fixed fee schedule in rule text reviewed - utility-specific
IN.ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Level 1 threshold (>10kW triggers Level 2/3 review)
IN.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (not a blanket statewide requirement identified in 170 IAC 4-4.3 sections reviewed)
IN.insurance_required: Liability insurance required per 170 IAC 4-4.3-10 for customer-owned generator equipment, maintained continuously while interconnected
IN.ic_timeline_days: Level 1: 10 business days to confirm completeness + 15 business days to approve/deny (statutory deadlines in 170 IAC 4-4.3-6); Level 2/3 timelines longer and utility-procedure-specific
