O certified non-export AC/DC converters; Rule 21 Non-Export agreement. NEM/NBT expansions above the 10%/1 kW limit can go on a Non-Export agreement without losing legacy status. Limited Generation Profiles (Res. E-5230 workshops) are an emerging path.
CA.storage_counts_toward_cap: No for the sized-to-load test, which uses renewable generator output only. Yes for the 1 MW threshold: Integrated or Directly Connected storage nameplate is added to aggregate facility nameplate (SCE Sched. NBT SC 1.b.iii.B). Large paired storage (>10 kW AC) is capped at 150% of the renewable generator's maximum output (D.19-01-030). D.20-06-017 suspended that cap from 2020-08-16; an Executive Director extension ran it to 2025-08-15. Whether the 150% cap is now enforced again is Unclear. Small paired storage (<=10 kW) has no relative size limit. SCE Sched. NBT SC 5.a.ii (Sheet 27, Advice 5228-E) says the waiver was extended by the Executive Director on 2023-09-05 and the 150% limit 'shall not apply until on and after August 16, 2025' - read literally the cap applies again from 2025-08-16; no later extension found, but not confirmed either. No limit on storage kWh.
CA.standby_charge: None for NEM/NBT generation: NEM customers are exempt from standby charges (CPUC NEM page), and SCE Sched. NBT Rates 5 says no Standby or Customer Generation Departing Load charges apply to the NBT generating facility's capacity. Non-eligible generators on the same premises are not exempt.

NC.rule_citation: N.C.G.S. 62-126.4 (H589, S.L. 2017-192); NCUC Docket E-100 Sub 180 Order Approving Revised Net Metering Tariffs (Mar 23 2023) + Order Granting Extension (May 17 2023) and Duke compliance tariffs filed Apr 3 2023 (DEC Leaf 72 Rider NM, Leaf 143 Rider NMB, Leaf 141 Rider RSC; DEP Riders NM-5, NMB-1, RSC-2); NC Interconnection Procedures (NCIP) eff. June 14 2019, Docket E-100 Sub 101 (text: https://www.duke-energy.com/_/media/pdfs/rates/ncinterconnections-dep.pdf?la=en)
NC.applies_to: IOU only (Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, Dominion Energy NC). EMCs and municipals are not rate-regulated by NCUC and are not required to offer net metering; they set their own rules (see utility file)
NC.nem_successor: Legacy Rider NM closed to new residential applicants (tariff text July 1 2023; extended to 9/30/2023 by May 17 2023 order); legacy residential participants must transfer to Rider NMB or another rider by Jan 1 2027. Successors: Rider RSC (Residential Solar Choice; requires Schedule R-TOU-CPP; netting within each TOU period incl. separate CPP period; NEEC for net excess; NBC; grid access fee above 15 kW; minimum bill) and Rider NMB (Net Metering Bridge; same credit/NBC/minimum bill but on any rate; annual kW enrollment caps; closed to new participants Jan 1 2027; Bridge Rate Period up to 15 calendar years from submission date of the applicable interconnection application, then transfer to RSC). Non-residential Rider NM not closed by these tariffs. BATTERY RETROFIT: riders require written notice of any Nameplate Capacity change within 60 days; neither NMB nor RSC text says a battery addition restarts the 15-yr Bridge term or forces a move to RSC - Unclear (a new interconnection application for the battery could arguably be 'the applicable interconnection application'; not addressed). MID-TRANSITION: legacy-to-NMB migration Jan 2027
NC.nem_cap_res_kw: 20 kW AC and not more than estimated maximum monthly demand of the residence (Riders NMB/RSC)
NC.nem_cap_nonres_kw: 1000 kW (legacy Rider NM, lesser of estimated max annual kW demand or 1,000 kW)
NC.nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide aggregate cap. Rider NMB annual enrollment capacity (kW AC, first-come first-served, reserved at interconnection application): DEC 2023 14,500 / 2024 31,900 / 2025 35,100 / 2026 38,700; DEP 2023 16,350 / 2024 35,900 / 2025 39,500 / 2026 43,500. Applicants after the annual cap must reapply next year or take RSC. Current subscription level not verified
NC.nem_sizing_rule: Residential (NMB/RSC): nameplate <= lesser of estimated max monthly demand of residence or 20 kW AC. Non-residential legacy NM: <= lesser of estimated max annual kW demand or 1,000 kW
NC.export_credit_value: Net Excess Energy Credit (NEEC): DEC 3.35 c/kWh, DEP 3.40 c/kWh (compliance tariffs eff. July 2023; later biennial updates not checked). Legacy Rider NM: 1:1 retail kWh (TOU customers netted by period)
NC.credit_rollover: Successor riders: monthly net excess credited in dollars at NEEC; credits roll forward (no forfeiture per installer summary). Legacy Rider NM: kWh credits roll monthly, forfeited annually
NC.annual_true_up: Legacy Rider NM only: unused credits forfeited June 1 (DEC) / May 31 (DEP) with no payment. Successor riders: no annual forfeiture (monthly NEEC crediting)
NC.ic_standard: NCIP (June 14 2019) Attachment 4: IEEE 1547 + IEEE 1547.1 testing, UL 1741 certified equipment (edition not specified). IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741-SB implementation tracked by annual utility reports in Docket E-100 Sub 101B (Duke report Apr 1 2020; DENC Mar 15 2021); a dated mandatory 1547-2018 cutover was not found
NC.ic_fast_track_kw: Certified UL inverter-based only. Line <5 kV: 100 kW (500 kW if on mainline and <=2.5 circuit miles from substation); 5-15 kV: 1 MW (2 MW); 15-35 kV: 2 MW; >=35 kV ineligible
NC.ic_simplified_kw: 20 kW (Section 2 20 kW Inverter Process for certified inverter-based facilities)
NC.ic_application_fee: $200 non-refundable (20 kW Inverter Process form, 2019 NCIP; 2015 NCIP was $100); Fast Track $750 (>20-100 kW), $1,000 (>100 kW-2 MW); Supplemental Review deposit $750 (>20-100 kW) and higher above; $500 pre-application report; $500 change of ownership; Study Process deposit + $1/kW AC capped at $100,000 aggregate
NC.ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Fast Track limits (100 kW-2 MW depending on line voltage/location), non-inverter or uncertified equipment, lines >=35 kV, or failure of Fast Track/Supplemental Review screens -> Section 4 Study Process (System Impact + Facilities studies)
NC.external_disconnect: Utility discretion (NCIP 6.16: utility may require lockable, visible, accessible manual load-break disconnect; for certified inverter-based <=10 kW where not otherwise code-required, utility reimburses reasonable cost)
NC.insurance_required: Residential <=250 kW: homeowner's policy with >= $100,000/occurrence liability; non-residential <=250 kW: CGL >= $300,000; non-residential >250 kW: CGL >= $1,000,000 (NCIP 6.15; self-insurance allowed if creditworthy)
NC.ic_timeline_days: 20 kW process: utility has 15 business days to verify screens; Fast Track initial review within 15 business days of complete request; witness test within 10 business days of Certificate of Completion
NC.storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (NCIP defines Generating Facility to include storage and asks kWh; adding storage/DC equipment not a Material Modification if output profile unchanged, NCIP 1.5.2. NEM riders admit only storage charged solely from onsite renewables)
NC.grid_charging_allowed: No - Riders NM, NMB and RSC (DEC and DEP) only admit 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from onsite renewable energy generation'. A grid-charged battery would have to sit outside net metering (non-NEM arrangement not verified)
NC.non_export_option: Partial: NCIP Interconnection Request asks for an hourly max import/export profile (flows above it = Adverse Operating Effect), and a Standby Generating Facility with zero export gets expedited Section 4 study (NCIP 1.8.3.4). No dedicated non-export Fast Track screen found
NC.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - 20 kW AC cap applies to 'Nameplate Capacity of Customer's installed generation system and equipment'; NBC/GAF billed per kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar; battery kW treatment not stated
NC.standby_charge: Not a standby charge per se: NBC $0.28/kW-mo (DEC) / $0.62/kW-mo (DEP) on nameplate; RSC Grid Access Fee $2.05 (DEC) / $1.50 (DEP) per kW above 15 kW; monthly minimum bill (customer+distribution portion) $22 (DEC NMB, DEC RSC, DEP NMB) / $28 (DEP RSC). DEP Rider NM-5: standby not required for residential or general service <=100 kW
NC.standby_threshold_kw: 15 kW (RSC grid access fee); 100 kW general service (DEP legacy NM standby waiver)

SC.jurisdiction_body: Public Service Commission of South Carolina (PSCSC); Office of Regulatory Staff
SC.rule_citation: S.C. Code 58-40-20 as amended by Act 62 of 2019 (SC Energy Freedom Act) - Solar Choice Metering; PSCSC Order 2021-390 (Duke, Docket 2020-264-E) and Order 2021-391 (DESC, Docket 2020-229-E); Order 2025-453 (DEC Rider NMT); SC Generator Interconnection Procedures eff. June 18 2021, Docket 2019-326-E, Order 2021-439 (https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/0d678dc4-2ccb-4938-8f9c-cf3982a3b781); DESC Solar Choice rider https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/36cec7b8-fe00-411a-87a1-320edcf87331; DEC Rider NMT https://etariff.psc.sc.gov/Uploads/tariffFile/ec070b41-9f5f-4c6f-a11a-480e0b73b559
SC.applies_to: IOU only (Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress, Dominion Energy South Carolina). Santee Cooper (state authority), electric cooperatives and munis are not bound by these tariffs and set their own net metering/interconnection rules (see utility file)
SC.nem_successor: Act 62 Solar Choice Metering tariffs for applications on/after June 1 2021: Duke Rider RSC (requires Schedule R-STOU; netting within each TOU period, CPP exports netted against On-Peak; net excess per TOU period credited at avoided-cost-based rate; NBC per kW; minimum bill); DESC Solar Choice rider to Rate 5 (TOU kWh netting by period, kWh bank to November; minimum term 10 yrs). Legacy Duke Rider RNM (1:1): applications before 5/16/2019 through 12/31/2025; 5/16/2019-5/31/2021 through 5/31/2029. MID-TRANSITION: DEC Rider NMT (Order 2025-453, eff. 1/1/2026) takes legacy RNM/IRSC customers for up to 10 yrs (to 12/31/2035 for pre-5/16/2019 apps; 6/1/2029-5/31/2039 for later apps) with monthly netting and NEEC for excess, then Rider RSC. BATTERY RETROFIT: NMT/RSC dates are keyed to the 'original interconnection application date for the generation system' and customers must report Nameplate Capacity changes within 60 days; neither rider says a battery addition resets dates - Unclear, but the storage-charging restriction below would apply
SC.nem_cap_res_kw: 20 kW AC (Act 62 customer-generator definition; Duke RSC/NMT and DESC Solar Choice riders)
SC.nem_aggregate_cap: None stated in the Solar Choice riders read (legacy DESC 2015 rider had a 0.2% of SC retail peak cap; that rider is closed)
SC.nem_sizing_rule: Customer-generator must be 'intended primarily to offset part or all of the customer-generator's own electrical energy requirements'; <=20 kW AC residential
SC.export_credit_value: DEC Rider RSC: $0.0397/kWh net excess per TOU period (Leaf 136 eff. 1/1/2024); DEC Rider NMT: 4.19 c/kWh (eff. 1/1/2026). DESC Solar Choice: excess kWh offsets same-TOU-period usage in later months; unused bank paid at avoided cost (Rate PR-1 off-peak winter energy credit) each November
SC.credit_rollover: Duke: monthly dollar credit at NEEC (no kWh bank). DESC: kWh bank rolls monthly within TOU period, cash-out at avoided cost in November
SC.annual_true_up: DESC: November billing cycle, unused excess kWh paid at avoided cost and bank zeroed. Duke RSC/NMT: none (monthly crediting)
SC.ic_standard: SC Generator Interconnection Procedures (June 18 2021) Attachment: IEEE 1547 + IEEE 1547.1 testing, UL certified inverters (edition not specified in text). No dated IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB mandate found
SC.ic_fast_track_kw: Certified UL inverter-based only. Line <5 kV: 100 kW (500 kW on mainline <=2.5 circuit miles from substation); 5-25 kV: 1 MW (2 MW); >=25 kV not eligible
SC.ic_simplified_kw: 20 kW (Section 2 20 kW Inverter Process; utility reserves circuit capacity per phase for <=20 kW projects)
SC.ic_application_fee: Fast Track/20 kW: $100 (<=20 kW), $250 (>20-100 kW), $500 (>100 kW-2 MW); $50 transfer of ownership; Study Process deposits separate (Duke cluster appendix $10,000 study deposit)
SC.ic_study_trigger_kw: Above Fast Track limits (100 kW-2 MW by voltage/location) or failure of Fast Track screens -> Section 4 serial Study Process, or Commission-authorized Cluster Study (utility appendix)
SC.external_disconnect: Required for 20 kW Inverter Process per its Terms and Conditions (manual load-break disconnect immediately adjacent to utility meter unless utility agrees otherwise); utility discretion above; utility reimburses cost for certified inverter-based <=10 kW when not code-required
SC.insurance_required: Residential <=250 kW: homeowner's policy >= $100,000/occurrence; non-residential <=250 kW: CGL >= $300,000; non-residential >250 kW higher (amount not read)
SC.ic_timeline_days: 20 kW process: utility has 15 business days to complete screening; witness test within 10 business days or deemed waived
SC.storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (customer-generator definition includes energy storage charged solely from onsite renewables; SC GIP application collects storage data)
SC.grid_charging_allowed: No - Act 62 customer-generator definition, repeated in Duke RSC/NMT and DESC Solar Choice riders, covers only 'an energy storage device configured to receive electrical charge solely from an onsite renewable energy resource'
SC.non_export_option: Unclear - no defined non-export/limited-export screen found in SC GIP text searched
SC.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear - 20 kW AC cap applies to 'Nameplate Capacity of Customer's installed generation system and equipment'; NBC billed on kW DC for solar or kW AC for non-solar
SC.standby_charge: No standby charge for Solar Choice residential. Duke: non-bypassable charge per nameplate kW (NMT: $0.45/kW for apps on/after 6/1/2021; RSC amount not read); NMT minimum customer & distribution charge $10; RSC minimum bill = Basic Facilities Charge plus rate-schedule minimum. DESC Solar Choice minimum bill $13.50/month

GA.jurisdiction_body: Georgia Public Service Commission (Georgia Power); EMC and municipal governing bodies for their own systems
GA.rule_citation: Georgia Cogeneration and Distributed Generation Act of 2001, O.C.G.A. 46-3-50 to 46-3-56; Georgia Power Schedule RNR-11 (eff. Jan 2023 bills; GPSC Dockets 4822 and 16573); Georgia Power Rules and Regulations Section G (Customer Generation) https://www.georgiapower.com/content/dam/georgia-power/pdfs/business-pdfs/tariffs/2023/Rules-Regs.pdf; GPC BTM Interconnection Summary (Residential) rev. 08.15.2025 https://www.georgiapower.com/content/dam/georgia-power/pdfs/company-pdfs/solar-pdfs/btm-distribution-interconnection-summary-residential.pdf
GA.applies_to: All utilities for the statutory purchase obligation ('electric service provider' includes electric utilities, EMCs and municipal utilities); PSC sets rates/interconnection terms only for Georgia Power; EMCs and munis set price and interconnection rules through their own governing bodies (46-3-56(b),(d))
GA.nem_successor: Georgia Power RNR-Monthly Netting (5,000-customer pilot) closed to new participants; non-transferable, 15-year term expiring no later than 12/31/2038, then automatic move to RNR-Instantaneous Netting. New customers: RNR-Instantaneous Netting (every kWh exported at any instant credited at Solar Avoided Energy Cost + 4 c/kWh adder)
GA.nem_cap_res_kw: 10 kW AC (statute and RNR; capacity = aggregate inverter nameplate at service point)
GA.nem_cap_nonres_kw: 100 kW (statute); Georgia Power RNR allows commercial up to 250 kW AC (100-250 kW limited to 125% of prior-year metered peak demand)
GA.nem_aggregate_cap: 0.2% of the utility's previous-year annual peak demand (O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(a); GPC RNR-Instantaneous first-come first-served to 0.2%); once subscribed, provider may purchase at a price set by PSC/governing body. Subscription level not verified
GA.nem_sizing_rule: GPC: 100-250 kW commercial <=125% of preceding year's metered peak demand; no residential consumption-based rule in RNR-11
GA.export_credit_value: GPC RNR-Instantaneous: Solar Avoided Energy Cost (updated annually under Renewable Cost Benefit framework, Docket 16573; value not read) + 4 c/kWh Renewable Generation Adder. RNR-Monthly (legacy): excess kWh offsets monthly consumption, remainder at Solar Avoided Energy Cost
GA.credit_rollover: Monthly: credits summed monthly and applied to that month's bill (carryover of credits exceeding the bill not stated in tariff)
GA.ic_standard: Georgia Power: Southern Company DER Parallel Operation policy; inverters and AC-coupled battery gateways must be listed UL 1741 SB and IEEE 1547-2018 (BTM Summary 2025); >=250 kW needs local communications interface per IEEE 1547-2018 (Rules and Regs G.3). Statute requires NEC/NESC/IEEE/UL compliance only
GA.ic_fast_track_kw: No statewide tiered fast-track; Georgia Power uses a single PowerClerk BTM process below 250 kW
GA.ic_application_fee: Georgia Power: one-time $100 residential, $200 commercial/industrial; for <250 kW covers review, metering/programming and witness testing (Rules and Regs G.4)
GA.ic_study_trigger_kw: 250 kW (Georgia Power: system impact study + witness testing mandatory at >=250 kW; smaller units only if deemed a risk)
GA.external_disconnect: Required by Georgia Power (one-line must show generation AC disconnect(s) isolating the facility, visible load-break details per Construction Guidelines); no statewide rule
GA.insurance_required: Statute bars providers from requiring additional liability insurance from a compliant customer generator (O.C.G.A. 46-3-56(e))
GA.storage_allowed: Yes-with-conditions (GPC: UL 1741 SB/IEEE 1547-2018 inverters; backup-capable systems need open-transition, mechanically interlocked transfer switch and DB 18-23 non-export form)
GA.grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - RNR-11 credits any metered 'Excess Energy' delivered to the grid and says nothing about battery charging source; GPC summary describes batteries for 'self-consumption only' use; no rule found that bars or permits crediting of grid-charged exports
GA.non_export_option: Yes - Georgia Power Energy Offset Only (EOO) agreement (no export, no compensation, utility may require export-prevention equipment; default if customer does not pick a program); DB 18-23 non-exporting generator form
GA.storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes (Georgia Power): AC capacity is aggregate inverter nameplate at the service point; a battery system with maximum inverter capability >10 kW (even if derated) makes a residential customer ineligible for RNR
GA.standby_charge: None found. RNR single-directional metering charge $5.97/mo (single-phase) or $12.66/mo (poly-phase) where used; bi-directional metering free

FL.applies_to: IOU only (FPL, Duke Energy Florida, Tampa Electric, FPUC). Municipals and co-ops are exempt from 25-6.065 but s. 366.91(6) F.S. requires each muni and retail co-op to adopt its own standardized interconnection agreement and net metering program (governing body sets terms; annual report to FPSC) -- see utility file deltas
FL.nem_successor: None. Full retail NEM survives; 2022 HB 741 (which would have phased NEM down) was vetoed. No open FPSC rulemaking to change 25-6.065 found as of 2026-09-24
FL.nem_sizing_rule: Gross power rating (AC = DC x 0.85) must not exceed 90% of customer's distribution service rating; rule sets no consumption-based cap, but utility guidelines add one (e.g. FPL <115% of annual kWh)
FL.export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail (monthly kWh carry-forward); annual cash-out at avoided cost
FL.export_credit_value: Monthly excess credited as kWh against next bill at retail; year-end unused credits paid at average annual rate of utility's COG-1 as-available energy tariff (utility-specific, not a single statewide value)
FL.credit_rollover: kWh credits roll monthly for up to 12 months; cash-out at avoided cost (COG-1) at end of calendar year and on account closure
FL.annual_true_up: End of each calendar year (December bill): unused kWh credits paid at average annual COG-1 as-available energy rate
FL.ic_standard: IEEE 1547 (2003) + IEEE 1547.1 (2005) + UL 1741 (2005) per rule text -- rule not updated for IEEE 1547-2018/UL 1741-SB; utility agreements cite IEEE 1547/UL 1741 current editions generically
FL.ic_fast_track_kw: 10 (Tier 1: no design review, no fees, no insurance); 100 (Tier 2: no further design review or extra equipment beyond disconnect)
FL.ic_application_fee: Tier 1: none allowed; Tier 2 and Tier 3: utility-proposed, FPSC-approved cost-based fee (e.g. FPL $400 Tier 2, $1,000 Tier 3); Tier 3 may add an Interconnection Study Charge
FL.ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier 3 >100 kW to 2 MW may require interconnection study)
FL.external_disconnect: Waived for inverter-based Tier 1 (unless installed at utility expense); utility may require visible-break lockable manual disconnect for Tier 2/3
FL.insurance_required: Tier 1: none (may be recommended); Tier 2: general liability up to $1M; Tier 3: up to $2M
FL.ic_timeline_days: 10 business days completeness notice; agreement executed within 30 calendar days of complete application (90 days if Tier 3 study); inspection within 30 days of executed agreement
FL.non_export_option: Not in rule. Stand-alone/grid-charged storage goes through the utility's Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (non-export -> no agreement needed at FPL if no utility equipment required)
FL.storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear (rule and tiers are defined on renewable gross power rating; battery not addressed in rule)
FL.standby_charge: Rule 25-6.065(8)(h): NEM customer continues to pay customer and demand charges; may at its discretion elect utility's standby/supplemental service rate. No mandatory standby charge on NEM customers
FL.standby_threshold_kw: N/A (no mandatory standby charge on NEM customers; standby rate optional per 25-6.065(8)(h))

AL.rule_citation: No statewide net metering or DG interconnection statute/rule. APSC-approved Alabama Power tariffs govern: Rate Rider RGB (Informal Docket U-4226, order 11/5/2021, eff. April 2022 billings); Rate PAE + Special Rules PAE (Docket 18005); APC DER Interconnection Process (July 2025) and DER Technical Interconnection Requirements Guidebook V3.2 (Feb 2026)
AL.applies_to: No statewide rule. APSC regulates Alabama Power only among retail utilities with DG tariffs; TVA-served munis/co-ops in north AL follow TVA (see TN row / Huntsville Utilities delta); non-TVA co-ops (PowerSouth members) and munis set their own terms
AL.nem_successor: No net metering at Alabama Power: exported energy bought at avoided cost under Rate PAE (<=100 kW; >100 kW Rate CPE contract); customer-generators must take Rate Rider RGB back-up service (capacity reservation charge)
AL.nem_cap_res_kw: N/A (no NEM). Rate PAE sellback available to facilities <=100 kW nameplate
AL.nem_cap_nonres_kw: N/A (no NEM). Rate PAE <=100 kW; larger via Rate CPE
AL.export_credit_value: Alabama Power Rate PAE (44th rev., eff. April 2023 billings, as posted): TOD option Jun-Sep 7.44c/kWh weekdays 10am-9pm CT, 5.23c other; Oct-May 4.86c weekdays 7am-9pm, 4.41c other. Time Advantage option 4.40-7.69c/kWh; FD-D option 4.41-6.73c/kWh. Monthly base charge $0.97 (1-ph) / $1.91 (3-ph)
AL.credit_rollover: PAE credits exceeding charges carried forward on account; check issued on customer request or termination
AL.ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018; UL 1741-SA or -SB listed inverters for Tier I/II, UL 1741-SB for Tier III (APC DER TIR Guidebook V3.2, Feb 2026)
AL.ic_fast_track_kw: 25 (Tier I, no study fee, 1-2 week review)
AL.ic_application_fee: Tier I <=25 kW: $0; Tier II >25-100 kW: $500; Tier III >100 kW: $1,000 screening fee (+ $300 optional pre-application; further studies ~$10k-$50k)
AL.ic_study_trigger_kw: 100 (Tier III screening; detailed distribution/transmission study if screen fails)
AL.external_disconnect: Required: manually operable, visible-break, lockable, 24/7-accessible AC disconnect isolating entire DER (Guidebook sec. 6.1)
AL.insurance_required: <=25 kW: recommended only; >25 kW: general liability >= $1M per incident naming APC as insured (Special Rules PAE rule 13)
AL.ic_timeline_days: No rule timeline; APC published targets: Tier I 1-2 wks, Tier II 2-4 wks, Tier III 4-12 wks (studies up to 26 wks). Design approval valid 365 days
AL.non_export_option: Yes: Guidebook defines Non-Export Generation (NEG) / Limited-Export Generation; Power Control Systems (UL 1741 CRD PCS or UL 3141) accepted for software export limits; >100 kW export limit set by impact study with backup export-limit relay. NEG still requires interconnection application and RGB applies
AL.storage_counts_toward_cap: Tiers set by total aggregate nameplate of DER energy conversion devices (batteries/inverters listed); whether battery inverter kW is added to PV kW for tiering and RGB nameplate billing: Unclear
AL.standby_charge: Rate Rider RGB (required for any customer with parallel non-emergency on-site generation): Capacity Reservation Charge $5.41/kW-month (secondary) or $4.87/kW-month (primary) on generator nameplate (customer may request calculated actual capacity need); alternative for qualifying residential customers: Rate RTA with 71c/kWh energy charge Jun-Sep weekdays 3-5pm in lieu of CRC. PURPA challenge: FERC declined enforcement 2021; M.D. Ala. granted summary judgment for APSC/Alabama Power 2026-03-25; appeal status not verified
AL.standby_threshold_kw: No size exemption: RGB applies to any parallel non-emergency generation (for customers on rates outside the listed schedules, generation must be <= lesser of 6% of max demand or 25 kW)

TN.jurisdiction_body: Tennessee Valley Authority (federal; sets terms for its local power companies via wholesale power contracts). Tennessee Public Utility Commission has no jurisdiction over TVA LPCs
TN.rule_citation: No Tennessee net metering or DG interconnection statute/rule. TVA Dispersed Power Production (DPP) Guidelines + Dispersed Power Price Schedule CSPP (PURPA avoided cost); TVA Green Connect program; each LPC interconnection agreement/policy
TN.applies_to: TVA-served LPCs (munis and co-ops = essentially all of TN). Each LPC sets its own interconnection agreement, fees, insurance and disconnect rules; TVA sets the export purchase terms (DPP). Kingsport Power (AEP, TPUC-regulated) not covered here
TN.nem_successor: Net metering not available in TVA service area (TVA Green Connect FAQ). Excess or all generation may be sold to TVA under DPP at avoided cost (5-year PPA with TVA; requires executed LPC interconnection agreement). TVA Green Power Providers (retail-plus premium) closed to new participants
TN.nem_cap_res_kw: N/A (no NEM). DPP accepts renewable QFs up to 80 MW
TN.export_credit_value: TVA DPP Schedule CSPP eff. 2025-12-01: Part A (meters <500 kW or not time-differentiated) 3.766c/kWh flat; Part B (>500 kW interval-metered): Super Peak 4.261, On Peak 4.212, Off Peak 3.736, Super Off Peak 3.538 c/kWh. Revised monthly-to-annually by TVA
TN.credit_rollover: None: DPP pays monthly via ACH for metered energy delivered to TVA (separately metered from LPC retail service)
TN.ic_standard: Set by each LPC (TVA requires anti-islanding trip <10 cycles in DPP PPA)
TN.ic_fast_track_kw: None at TVA level (tiers, if any, set by each LPC)
TN.ic_simplified_kw: None at TVA level (tiers, if any, set by each LPC)
TN.ic_study_trigger_kw: 250 (TVA transmission screening for DPP facilities >250 kW; TVA transmission study if screen fails or >5 MVA)
TN.insurance_required: TVA requires none; many LPCs do (per TVA Green Connect FAQ)
TN.ic_timeline_days: No TVA-level timeline; set by each LPC (e.g. MLGW technical review ~4-5 weeks; NES application due >=60 days before operation)
TN.non_export_option: Yes in practice: behind-the-meter self-consumption without DPP enrollment still needs LPC interconnection agreement; non-export path rules set per LPC
TN.standby_charge: None at TVA level; LPC-specific (TVA wholesale rate structure lets LPCs add grid-access/fixed charges)
TN.standby_threshold_kw: N/A at TVA level (LPC-specific, e.g. MLGW availability charge on all self-generators)
